items.title: Líder de secta en Kenia que imponía ayuno extremo es declarado culpable matar a 191 niños
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Un tribunal de Kenia declaró el lunes culpable al líder de la secta de la inanición, Paul Mackenzie, y a otras 30 personas, de asesinato, por la muerte de 190 niños y un adulto en uno de los peores desastres relacionados con sectas de la historia reciente.
items.body:
Un tribunal de Kenia declaró el lunes culpable al líder de la secta de la inanición, Paul Mackenzie, y a otras 30 personas, de asesinato, por la muerte de 190 niños y un adulto en uno de los peores desastres relacionados con sectas de la historia reciente.
Mackenzie fue detenido en 2023 tras una denuncia recibida por la policía, y semanas más tarde las autoridades comenzaron a hallar cadáveres en fosas comunes en el bosque de Shakahola, cerca de la costa del sureste de Kenia.
La fiscalía acusó a Mackenzie y su Iglesia Internacional de las Buenas Nuevas de organizar una secta cristiana apocalíptica en la que ordenaban a sus seguidores que se dejaran morir de hambre a sí mismos y a sus hijos para ir al cielo antes del fin del mundo.
Mackenzie negó los cargos de asesinato, alegando que no obligó a las víctimas a morir de hambre, pero el tribunal rechazó el argumento.
En total, se han recuperado más de 400 cadáveres del bosque de Shakahola. Muchos se encontraban en avanzado estado de descomposición, por lo que solo se pudieron identificar 26 cadáveres.
La sentencia del lunes abarcó 191 fallecimientos, mientras que las investigaciones sobre las demás muertes siguen abiertas.
FAMILIAS ESCUCHAN EL VEREDICTO EN EL TRIBUNAL La jueza Diana Kavedza Mochache dijo en una vista, que duró más de ocho horas, que, en algunos casos, se aisló a los niños y se les negó la comida mientras sus padres observaban.
Mackenzie se encontraba en la sala, vestido con una camiseta a rayas y pantalones rojos, sentado junto a su esposa, que también está acusada.
Permaneció en silencio, con la mirada perdida, antes de que se dictara la sentencia.
Los familiares de algunas de las personas que fallecieron en el bosque se reunieron para escuchar la sentencia en el Tribunal Superior de Mombasa.
Francis Wanje, de 62 años, perdió a ocho familiares, entre ellos dos nietos, a manos de la secta.
"Ha sido algo realmente duro para nosotros como familia, y nos ha afectado mucho en términos de problemas psicológicos (...) Estaba esperando este día", dijo antes de la audiencia.
La tragedia de Shakahola ha conmocionado a Kenia desde el descubrimiento de fosas comunes en el bosque costero hace más de tres años.
Personas con conocimiento directo de las actividades de la secta explicaron a Reuters que Mackenzie planeó la inanición masiva en tres fases: primero los niños, luego las mujeres y los jóvenes, y finalmente el resto de los hombres.
Mackenzie, un antiguo taxista, prohibió a los miembros de la secta enviar a sus hijos al colegio y acudir al hospital cuando estaban enfermos, tachando a dichas instituciones de satánicas, contaron algunos de sus seguidores a Reuters en 2023.

items.title: How the gold boom is fuelling tree loss from Ghana to the Amazon
items.author: Mark Hillsdon
items.creator: Mark Hillsdon
items.summary: As the price of gold booms, so does the roar of excavators and scream of chainsaws in some of the world’s most ecologically sensitive forests.
items.body:
As the price of gold booms, so does the roar of excavators and scream of chainsaws in some of the world’s most ecologically sensitive forests.
Between 2001 and 2019, gold drove more deforestation than any other mineral, from the dense tropical forests of the Amazon and Africa’s western coast, to the boreal forests of Russia, and down through Myanmar and Indonesia.
But with prices having spiked more than 120% in the last five years, fuelled by geopolitical instability and disruptions to international trade, campaigners fear the gold rush has only accelerated, with huge implications for the world’s forests.
“The rapid rise in the price of gold creates a powerful economic incentive for mining expansion,” explains Andres Santana, senior manager for combating illegal deforestation at Amazon Conservation, in an email.
“Higher prices increase the potential returns from extracting gold, including from remote and environmentally sensitive areas, adding further pressure to forests and local communities.”
Criminal gangs have moved in as gold’s price has risen, funding illegal mining and taking advantage of gold’s mercurial properties; it’s ability to be re-smelted creates a shape-shifting currency that is hard to trace, and easy to launder. As Reuters has reported , gold smuggling out of Africa has surged over the past decade, finding its way onto international markets through regional hubs in Mali, and less regulated markets in Dubai, Istanbul and Mumbai. It’s these loopholes that campaigners want the industry to close.
Hannah Mowat, campaigns coordinator at the environmental NGO Fern, says in an email that in many countries “small-scale illicit mining is largely controlled by big players, who operate with foreign money and have top political connections. These are not artisanal miners panning for gold – these are highly mechanised, highly financialised and connected actors.”
A specialist handles ingots of 99.99% pure gold. The price of gold has spiked more than 120% in the last five years, fuelled by geopolitical instability and trade disruptions. REUTERS/Alexander Manzyuk Not only does this illicit mining cause deforestation, but the use of mercury and cyanide poisons water supplies and food chains, leading to severe health consequences for communities living downstream of mining sites.
On a recent visit to Ghana, Jonathan Byers, a consultant and geospatial analyst at the environmental NGO Mighty Earth saw entire river valleys where the water flowed milky brown due to pollution from gold mining. “They can’t even put (it) on the cocoa trees anymore because it kills them,” he explains. “It is the human impacts of this that are pretty catastrophic.”
While industrial gold mining has been linked with harm to communities through deforestation and pollution , major international mining companies must comply with strict rules to be members of organisations such as the World Gold Council (WGC), whose Responsible Gold Mining Principles sets a framework for the gold supply chain, including investors and consumers.
Another initiative is the Gold Bar Integrity (GBI) programme, run jointly by the WGC and the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA). It uses blockchain technology to digitally trace gold as it moves through global supply chains, with refineries having to report the country of origin for every gram of gold they take in, explains Neil Harby, LBMA's chief technical officer. Applying the so-called alchemy test, he says, “means a refinery cannot … produce more gold bars than the gold it sourced”.
Around 90% of industrially mined gold (sanctions mean Russia is excluded) are covered by the GBI, but the standard only takes in a small fraction of gold from artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), even though this accounts for as much as 20% of global production. While not all ASGM gold is illegal, “this is where the deforestation is happening,” says Harby.
The rising price of gold has also increased the demand for scrap and recycled gold, says Harby, which now makes up as much as 50% of the gold market. The link between recycled and ASGM gold is strong, he says. “It (ASGM gold) gets passed as recycled gold; it loses its identity, what we call ‘gold-washing’.”
Chemically finger-printing the gold can help. “Gold from certain countries has certain signatures,” says Harby, “but, as this gold is re-smelted time and time again, it becomes increasingly difficult to track these trace elements.”
Jewellery made from gold is smelted down at a factory. The rising price of gold has increased the demand for recycled gold, which now makes up as much as 50% of the gold market. REUTERS/Vasily Fedosenko Ghana is suffering more than most from illicit mining, and is now one of the most heavily mined countries in the world. In 2022, the then government passed legislation opening up nearly 90% of the country’s 9 million hectares of forest reserves to mining. One study found a 5.9% decline in forest cover in one reserve, which had experienced a 19-fold increase in mining, and a complete absence of vegetation in areas that were heavily mine.
This led to the creation of the Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey, explains Daryl Bosu, deputy director at the conservation NGO A Roche Ghana. Galamsey roughly translates as “gather and sell”, he says, when historically people could pick gold nuggets from riverbeds or fields after heavy rainfall.
In 2025 a new government repealed the law but Bosu says the reality on the ground is unchanged. “Our forests reserves are still under rampage and destruction by illegal miners.”
Last year the Ghanian government set up the Gold Board (Goldbod) to clamp down on criminal gangs who were smuggling gold out of Ghana.
But the system doesn’t address traceability, says Bosu. He has no doubt that gold linked to deforestation in Ghana continues to reach London markets (which account for 70% of global trade).
He wants a zero-tolerance approach towards miners and politicians involved in illegal mining, and in this respect can see a glimmer of hope. In July, politician and businessman politician Bernard Antwi Boasiako was jailed for 20 years for involvement in illegal mining. At the same time, Ghana and the WGC signed an agreement to accelerate the formalisation of the country’s ASGM sector, with a mixture of investment and training.
Another area on the frontline of expanding gold mining is the Amazon. According to March’s inaugural report of the Amazon Mining Watch Panorama, in the last quarter of 2025 there was an estimated 6,000 ha of new mining-related deforestation (MRD) across the Amazon Basin, much of it put down to the quest for gold.
A cocoa farmer, visits her cocoa plantation destroyed by illegal gold mining in the Samreboi community in the Western Region, Ghana, February 26, 2024. REUTERS/Francis Kokoroko Amazon Mining Watch is a platform led by Amazon Conservation, Earth Genome and the Pulitzer Center.
The report used AI to analyse mining scars across all nine Amazonian countries, and showed that as well as new incursions in areas such as Territorio Charip in Ecuador, there was a resurgence of activity in the Igarapes do Juruena State Park in Brazil, where MRD rose by 660% between August 2025 and April 2026.
A further 200 ha of MRD were detected in Peru’s Tambopata National Reserve, which had seen levels of forest destruction drop after a major government operation.
“Criminal organisations can exploit weak… gold traceability systems and gaps in due diligence requirements to introduce illegally extracted gold into legal supply chains,” says Amazon Conservation’s Santana, “taking advantage of the Amazon’s vast geography, institutional weaknesses and limited regional coordination.”
Amazon Conservation has also launched the Amazon Mining Policy Scoreboard, which evaluates and compares the legal and policy frameworks governing gold mining across the Amazon.
It shows that many countries have strong legal frameworks on paper, but implementation lags, with governments failing to address the underlying drivers of illegal mining, as well as providing alternative livelihoods for communities.
Victoire Girard, a professor at the Nova School of Business and Economics at the New University of Lisbon, says illegal mining provides a livelihood for millions of people, which means a simple ban on illicit gold mining won’t work.
An illegal wildcat gold mine in an area of deforested Amazon rainforest in Para State, Brazil. REUTERS/Nacho Doce “People are attracted to gold mining because they can’t do anything else,” she explains. “If there’s a drought and cultivators lose everything, they’re going to turn to gold as an alternative livelihood.”
There’s already a growing trend in Ghana for farmers to grub up their uneconomic cocoa plantations and mine the land instead, she says. To keep the farmers working the land rather than mining it, she believes, companies and governments need to look at issues such as crop insurance and affordable loans.
Mowat of FERN agrees there will always be some form of mining, and that communities “must get increased income and wealth from the gold that they are digging out”. This includes having a greater say in the allocation of mining permits, more community benefits and better training of artisanal miners.
The WGC also recognises the problem. The council’s global head of public policy, Andrew Naylor, said in an email that while governments have the primary responsibility to enforce laws and improve governance industry and civil society can help by building formal pathways for legitimate ASGM gold to enter the market.
“Enforcement is necessary to disrupt criminal networks, but formalisation is what helps prevent them from returning,” he adds.
Mowat acknowledges the work that organisations such as the WGC are doing, but points out that its rules are voluntary, and there’s no external scrutiny.
In December, London hosts the Illicit Finance Summit, when FERN and other civil society organisations will present a roadmap to address illegal mining’s root causes. Alongside tackling the systemic poverty driving small-scale miners into illicit supply chains, it will also encourage financial centres to do more to ensure that illegal gold can’t be co-mingled with legitimate gold and enter the international financial system.
“Unless there is a clear, international standard for responsible gold, that requires market players to know where the gold they are dealing with comes from, then western markets will continue to drive illicit gold mining, and fuel global insecurity, human rights abuses and environmental harm,” Mowat adds.
This article is from the latest issue of The Ethical Corporation magazine, on deforestation risk. You can download the digital pdf of the magazine by clicking here

items.title: Italie-Les boutiques de Milan ont fermé plus tôt, craintes de nouveaux pillages
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les magasins du centre de Milan ont fermé plus tôt que d'habitude lundi et ont barricadé leurs vitrines, craignant de nouveaux troubles après deux jours de manifestations au cours desquels des groupes de personnes cagoulées se sont affrontés avec la police, ont pillé des magasins et saccagé des biens.
items.body:
Les magasins du centre de Milan ont fermé plus tôt que d'habitude lundi et ont barricadé leurs vitrines, craignant de nouveaux troubles après deux jours de manifestations au cours desquels des groupes de personnes cagoulées se sont affrontés avec la police, ont pillé des magasins et saccagé des biens.
La plupart des boutiques de luxe de la Via Montenapoleone, où sont implantées des marques telles que Chanel, Tiffany et Dior, ont retiré leurs articles de vitrine par mesure de précaution.
La police italienne a interpellé 271 individus lors des troubles survenus dimanche à Milan, ont déclaré lundi les autorités, après des violences en marge d'une deuxième journée de manifestations contre la dégradation des services publics et la hausse du coût de la vie.
Des enseignes de sport telles que Decathlon et Arc'teryx ou encore celle de téléphonie Vodafone ont été pillées, au cours de ces vioolences, selon des images diffusées à la télévision.
Parmi les personnes emmenées au poste de police, trente-deux ont été placées en garde à vue, dont vingt-trois mineurs et treize ressortissants étrangers. Vingt-huit autres individus ont été déférés devant les autorités judiciaires.
Ces incidents font suite à des affrontements similaires survenus samedi dans des villes du nord, notamment Bologne, Brescia, Bergame et Turin, où vingt-huit manifestants ont été arrêtés, selon la police.
La présidente du Conseil Giorgia Meloni, dont la coalition de droite est, selon les sondages, loin d'être donnée favorite pour les élections nationales de 2027, a condamné ces violences et a présidé lundi une réunion avec ses ministres et les responsables de la sécurité afin d’examiner la situation.
Le gouvernement prévoit d’adopter des mesures proposées par la police visant à prévenir et à lutter contre de telles flambées de violence, a déclaré une source gouvernementale, ajoutant que ces propositions seraient soumises lors d’une réunion du Conseil des ministres prévue mardi.
Selon le Corriere della Sera, Giorgia Meloni envisage ainsi de rallonger la détention préventive pour les mineurs et de sévir contre les gangs de jeunes.

items.title: Saudi Arabia postpones its 'Davos in the Desert' conference after attacks
items.author: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni, Tala Ramadan, Alexander Cornwell
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni, Tala Ramadan, Alexander Cornwell
items.summary: Saudi Arabia has decided to postpone its flagship investment conference until next year, organizers confirmed in a statement on Monday, following deadly attacks which rocked the kingdom in recent weeks as the Middle East conflict widens, disrupting business.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia has decided to postpone its flagship investment [USN:L6N4600CJ TEXT:"conference"] until next year, organizers confirmed in a statement on Monday, following deadly attacks which rocked the kingdom in recent weeks as the Middle East conflict widens, disrupting business.
The Future Investment Initiative, or FII, was planned for October 26 to 29, but will now take place in 2027, with a new date to be announced "very soon," the organizers said. Reuters [USN:L6N4650WL TEXT:"reported"] earlier Monday that the in-person event had been scrapped and organizers were weighing postponing the event.
The conference, set for its 10th edition, has become a must-attend event for some of the world's top financiers. Informally dubbed "Davos in the Desert," in a nod to the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Switzerland, the state-backed annual event has showcased the kingdom's ambitious investment plans in a bid to attract billions of dollars needed to fund its economic transformation away from hydrocarbons towards tourism, sports and technology.
Expected speakers for this year's event included Goldman Sachs (GS.N) CEO and Chairman David Solomon, Standard Chartered (STAN.L) CEO Bill Winters and Citi's CEO Jane Fraser, according to a draft programme.
The US-Israeli war with Iran this year has disrupted the Gulf's busy calendar of events, with several conferences cancelled, postponed or retooled in the UAE and Qatar in the first part of the year, when the countries bore the brunt of the attacks while Saudi Arabia suffered [USN:L6N42B0X9 TEXT:"fewer"] hits.
The kingdom in recent weeks has faced an escalating war with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, which have [USN:L6N4600NM TEXT:"struck"] military, energy and civilian infrastructure across the country, including state oil company Aramco's headquarters and Riyadh's international airport, where strikes [USN:L8N45X021 TEXT:"killed"] at least 18 people and hundreds were wounded this month.
FII said it wanted to ensure the event delivered "the full scale, extraordinary quality, and unforgettable impact that our community has come to expect."
Reuters reported last week that the FII organizers considered a hybrid format, allowing executives to tune in remotely. Semafor reported Monday that big banks and private-equity firms have privately relayed safety concerns about attending the event to Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan, adding that CEOs feel pressure to attend the four-day event.
items.raw_description: Saudi Arabia has decided to postpone its flagship investment conference until next year, organizers confirmed in a statement on Monday, following deadly attacks which rocked the kingdom in recent weeks as the Middle East conflict widens, disrupting business.

items.title: Eyes in the skies: How satellites are boosting confidence in forest carbon projects
items.author: Ben Payton
items.creator: Ben Payton
items.summary: Once every three days, as the European Space Agency’s Biomass satellite races across the sky at a speed of 27,000 kilometres per hour, it passes over a specific point within the Congo rainforest, the mighty expanse of greenery in the heart of Africa. As it completes this circuit, the satellite beams data back to Earth, allowing scientists to piece together a 3D scan to monitor the health of the forest.
items.body:
Once every three days, as the European Space Agency’s Biomass satellite races across the sky at a speed of 27,000 kilometres per hour, it passes over a specific point within the Congo rainforest, the mighty expanse of greenery in the heart of Africa. As it completes this circuit, the satellite beams data back to Earth, allowing scientists to piece together a 3D scan to monitor the health of the forest.
Biomass, launched from French Guiana in April 2025, is one of a growing number of satellites tasked with surveying the Earth’s forests. Uniquely, it uses P-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR). By transmitting ultra-long radio waves that penetrate the forest canopy, the satellite can measure tree trunks and branches, which provides a proxy for the amount of carbon being stored.
Satellites like Biomass are “absolutely essential” for rainforest conservation, says Donna Lyndsay, climate services development manager at Space4Climate, a public-private partnership that promotes the use of satellite data for climate action.
She notes that cutting-edge satellites are now orbiting the Earth at a greater cadence, providing increasingly high-resolution spatial imagery that can offer early warning signs of any deterioration in forest health.
As the pace of climate change escalates, monitoring threats to tropical forests – and, ultimately, intervening to counter these threats – has never been so important.
L-band SAR, a less advanced technology than P-band, has been key to helping scientists realise that Africa’s forests and woody savannahs have already passed a tipping point.
According to findings published in the journal Scientific Reports , rapid deforestation means these African biomes have been releasing more carbon than they sequester since 2010.
Logs lie next to a rusting barge on the banks of the Congo river. REUTERS/David Lewis Alongside continuous innovation in the hardware of satellites, breakthroughs on the software side are enabling scientists to make ever-greater use of satellite data.
“We have now, through the use of AI capabilities, the ability to really interrogate these datasets on a massive scale,” says Lyndsay. This is paving the way for a significant expansion in predictive analytics, she says. A company might, for example, receive an alert that signals of impending deforestation have been detected within areas from which its sources commodities. Armed with this data, the company could then consider taking preventative action.
The Congo rainforest stretches across Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Congo-Brazzaville, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon, as well as DR Congo itself. With much of its expanse virtually inaccessible by road, Satellites offer the only practical way of keeping track of deforestation threats.
“I don't think there's any way that we could possibly have oversight of all natural forests globally, without having some sort of bird’s-eye view of what's going on,” says Lucy Barnes, a senior manager for supply chain solutions at the Earthworm Foundation. The non-profit has been running a satellite monitoring platform called Starling with Airbus since 2016 that can alert major companies to risks of deforestation in their supply chains.
Improved technology will open new possibilities for using satellite data, Barnes adds. “It's not necessarily about using it just for monitoring deforestation, as such. I think in some ways, we’re able to do that to a very high level now. It's how you can also use that data for answering other environmental questions, for example, measuring carbon sequestration.”
Indeed, multiple actors in the carbon markets space are already making extensive use of satellite data. The hope is that satellite data could even help solve some of the longstanding problems that have undermined the growth of these markets.
REDD+ carbon credit schemes have been heavily promoted as a way to avoid emissions linked to deforestation, yet these schemes have repeatedly been criticised for alleged “over-crediting”.
An image of Sumatra in western Indonesia via Starling, a satellite monitoring platform run by Earthworm Foundation and Airbus. Starling/Handout via REUTERS In a notorious example, project developer Carbon Green Investments and environmental consultancy South Pole grossly overstated the rate of deforestation in a “reference area” close to the forest they were seeking to preserve through the Kariba REDD+ project in Zimbabwe.
This allowed the developer to claim its interventions within the project area made a greater impact in avoiding emissions than was truly the case. Following a lengthy investigation, carbon markets registry Verra found last year that the project had issued more than twice as many credits as it should have done.
In the wake of these reputational disasters, the price of avoided deforestation credits remains depressed. Even higher-rated REDD+ credits trade at only around $7 per tonne, according to data from carbon markets intelligence firm Sylvera. By comparison, high-rated projects that remove carbon through reforestation or afforestation average $26.10 per tonne.
Yet experts agree that there is no higher priority for climate and biodiversity than protecting existing forest habitats. In other words, there is a misalignment in the market between the financial value of afforestation versus the conservation value of avoiding deforestation in the first place.
Satellite monitoring could help solve this conundrum. Phil Platts, senior vice president for geospatial and Earth observation at carbon ratings agency BeZero Carbon, notes that newer avoided deforestation methodologies – such as Verra’s VM0048 – take responsibility for determining the baseline used to calculate deforestation rates away from project developers.
Instead, registries use satellite imagery to calculate deforestation rates across a country or province; credit issuance is then based on comparing deforestation in the project area with the wider jurisdiction.
The “systematic over-crediting” that once marred avoided deforestation projects “just isn’t there with these new methodologies,” Platts says.
Finland-based ICEYE is partnering with the Jane Goodall Foundation to support chimpanzee conservation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo by using SAR to detect logging and illegal mining. REUTERS/James Akena Despite these advances, the carbon markets remain controversial. Rainforest Foundation UK’s executive director Joe Eisen describes the market as a “folly” in the forests of central Africa, warning that revenues are “not filtering down to communities where it's most needed”.
Nevertheless, Rainforest Foundation UK is working on a pilot project in 30 community forests in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in which communities receive payments based on protecting forest cover. The verification of results is “based entirely on satellite data”, Eisen says.
The NGO also operates a satellite monitoring platform called ForestEye, which can provide community forest monitoring groups with access to intelligence on disturbance to the forest canopy.
As both hardware and software continues to improve, satellite technology will play an increasingly key role both in monitoring forest carbon projects, and in supporting rainforest conservation more generally.
One company pushing the boundaries of what satellite monitoring can do is ICEYE, a Finland-headquartered company that operates the world’s largest constellation of SAR satellites.
In April, it announced a partnership with the Jane Goodall Foundation to support chimpanzee conservation in eastern DRC by using SAR to detect threats such as logging and illegal mining.
Michael Bennett, ICEYE’s head of government solutions, says conventional satellite monitoring is insufficient in this region, which is blanketed by thick clouds for much of the year. Illegal activities can easily remain undetected beneath the thick forest canopy.
DRC has been losing roughly 0.5% of its primary forests each year over the past decade, largely due to encroachment of small-scale agriculture. REUTERS/Arlette Bashizi “With SAR, you don't need to get lucky,” he says. Much like the ESA’s Biomass satellite, the radar beams transmitted by ICEYE’s satellites can penetrate both cloud and canopy cover to build a 3D image that make it easier to detect possible threats.
And while conservation organisations might traditionally rely on satellite images that are several months, or even years, out of date, Bennett stresses that ICEYE’s constellation of dozens of satellites in low Earth orbit mean the company can provide “near-real time” coverage.
Of course, gaining these kinds of insights is only the first step. There is still the problem of how to intervene in an environment where the government’s authority is limited at best.
With a more accurate picture of threats to chimpanzees, however, Bennett suggests the Jane Goodall Foundation will be able to become more proactive in alerting authorities and on-the-ground team to the need for action.
Sassan Saatchi is CEO of CTrees, a platform that offers free access to data on carbon sequestration down to the level of an individual tree. While hailing the advances in satellite technology, he says more work is needed to ensure that increasingly abundant sources of data are actually used by local teams, both in carbon projects and in broader conservation efforts. “There is so much free material and technology they can use,” he says. “If they use it, it would be a significant change.”
The dangers facing the great forests of central Africa and their wealth of biodiversity remain formidable. DRC has been losing roughly 0.5% of its primary forests each year over the past decade, largely due to encroachment of small-scale agriculture. And Cameroon suffered its worst ever year of deforestation in 2025, partly driven by the growth of cocoa plantations.
Thanks to satellite data, governments, NGOs and companies have a clearer picture than ever before on the health of Africa’s forests. The challenge now, with the help of satellite tools, is to find ways to ensure these green lungs can survive forever.
This article is from the latest issue of The Ethical Corporation magazine, on deforestation risk. You can download the digital pdf of the magazine by clicking here

items.title: Neue Regierung Ungarns plant deutliche Senkung des Haushaltsdefizits
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ungarn strebt für das kommende Jahr eine deutliche Senkung seines Haushaltsdefizits auf 4,9 Prozent des Bruttoinlandsprodukts (BIP) an. Den entsprechenden Haushaltsentwurf stellte Ministerpräsident Peter Magyar am Montag vor. Das Vorhaben gilt als wichtiger Prüfstein für die Glaubwürdigkeit des Ziels, den Euro einzuführen. Die geplante Verringerung wäre ein deutlicher Rückgang gegenüber dem für dieses Jahr erwarteten Defizit von 7,5 Prozent. Zudem ist das Ziel ehrgeiziger als die von Analysten in einer Reuters-Umfrage prognostizierten 5,3 Prozent.
items.body:
Ungarn strebt für das kommende Jahr eine deutliche Senkung seines Haushaltsdefizits auf 4,9 Prozent des Bruttoinlandsprodukts (BIP) an. Den entsprechenden Haushaltsentwurf stellte Ministerpräsident Peter Magyar am Montag vor. Das Vorhaben gilt als wichtiger Prüfstein für die Glaubwürdigkeit des Ziels, den Euro einzuführen. Die geplante Verringerung wäre ein deutlicher Rückgang gegenüber dem für dieses Jahr erwarteten Defizit von 7,5 Prozent. Zudem ist das Ziel ehrgeiziger als die von Analysten in einer Reuters-Umfrage prognostizierten 5,3 Prozent.
Magyar versucht, das Defizit mittelfristig unter die EU-Obergrenze von drei Prozent - eines der Euro-Kriterien - zu drücken, ohne dabei seine Wahlversprechen zu brechen. Er hatte im April einen Erdrutschsieg über Viktor Orban errungen. Die geplanten Mehrausgaben sollen im kommenden Jahr mehr als zwei Billionen Forint (rund 5,7 Milliarden Euro) betragen. Gleichzeitig will die Regierung Einsparungen von 1,5 Billionen Forint (rund 3,8 Milliarden Euro) vornehmen. Die Einnahmen sollen durch eine neue Vermögenssteuer, eine höhere Körperschaftssteuer für Großkonzerne sowie höhere Steuern für Energieunternehmen gesteigert werden.
Der Entwurf sieht zudem Steuersenkungen für mehr als zwei Millionen Steuerzahler im Umfang von 250 Milliarden Forint (rund 625 Millionen Euro) vor. Der Einkommensteuersatz auf den Mindestlohn soll auf neun Prozent sinken. Das Ziel der Euro-Einführung hatte zuletzt zu einer Aufwertung des ungarischen Forint beigetragen, was die Inflation unter das Inflationsziel der Zentralbank drückte. Die Renditen für Staatsanleihen fielen auf einen der niedrigsten Werte in Mitteleuropa. Am Montag legte der Forint gegenüber anderen Währungen der Region zu und erreichte den höchsten Stand seit vier Wochen. Analysten rechnen mit einem Beitritt Ungarns zur Eurozone in den Jahren 2032 oder 2033.

items.title: Energy Watch: Elections angst
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Elections are always delicate moments. With Israel's parliamentary vote eight days away and the US midterms following a week later, oil markets are nervously watching the Middle East. Reported Iranian attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz reached a record 12 last week, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency.
items.body:
Elections are always delicate moments. With [USN:FWN4630MG TEXT:"Israel's parliamentary vote"] eight days away and the [USN:L1N4600TJ TEXT:"US midterms"] following a week later, oil markets are nervously watching the Middle East. Reported [USN:S8N45501B TEXT:"Iranian attacks"] on ships around the Strait of Hormuz reached a record 12 last week, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency.
What was most telling was not the number itself but the fact that UKMTO admitted that it is struggling to keep count of strikes, "with the majority of vessels attacked refusing to report."
This surge in attacks appears to be having a significant impact on flows. Oil exports through the narrow waterway have fallen from a peak of 17 million barrels per day in early October to around 11 million bpd in recent days, Kpler data showed. Yet producers and shippers are still sailing through Hormuz, showing how quickly the industry has adapted to a new normal characterized by severely heightened risk.
That resilience comes at a cost, however.
Just ask Asian refiners. They purchase the majority of the Middle East's oil, and soaring shipping costs are crushing their profit margins. For more on that, [USN:L6N4620UK TEXT:"check out my latest column"].
Oil prices, meanwhile, hit a 5-month high of over $109 a barrel on Friday, reflecting growing angst among investors that the Iran war could reignite, with President Donald Trump saying the US might [USN:L6N4620Q7 TEXT:"renew strikes"] on Iran's nuclear facilities. Benchmark Brent oil prices slipped on Monday, however.
In other news:
China's economy [USN:L1N46501H TEXT:"bounced back"] from a three-year low, growing 4.5% in the third quarter and beating forecasts as roaring exports offset consumers' tight grip on their wallets. The strong reading is another sign that the world's top oil importer has largely shielded itself from the worst effects of the Iran war.
Chinese oil refineries raised processing rates slightly in September for a third straight month as strong fuel exports supported demand. The world's biggest oil buyer cut crude imports by 21.5% from a year earlier while boosting domestic production.
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney is betting that a new pipeline can revive the country's oil industry, lift production and exports, and reduce the country’s dependence on the United States. Bringing back jobs will be much harder, writes Reuters correspondent Amanda Stephenson.
The US and Israeli war against Iran has dominated the energy story in 2026. But the quiet retooling of power grids from Lagos to Manila may prove [USN:L1N45Z15T TEXT:"more significant"] in the long run, writes ROI Energy Transition Columnist Gavin Maguire.
As ever, don't hesitate to contact me at ron.bousso@thomsonreuters.com or follow me on LinkedIn with any questions or thoughts.
Subscribe to get Ron Bousso's Power Up newsletter delivered to your inbox every Monday and Thursday.
Opinions expressed are those of the author. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

items.title: Menino de 13 anos é suspeito de esfaquear professora e aluno na Romênia após publicações no TikTok
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A polícia romena informou que um estudante de 13 anos esfaqueou e feriu uma professora e outro aluno na segunda-feira, em meio a relatos da mídia local de que ele havia postado sobre seus planos nas redes sociais pouco antes do ataque.
items.body:
A polícia romena informou que um estudante de 13 anos esfaqueou e feriu uma professora e outro aluno na segunda-feira, em meio a relatos da mídia local de que ele havia postado sobre seus planos nas redes sociais pouco antes do ataque.
As escolas na Europa têm enfrentado uma série de ataques este ano em países como Polônia, França e Suécia, com as autoridades, em alguns casos, apontando o papel das redes sociais e das subculturas online que glorificam o assassinato como fator que incita a violência.
“Por volta das 8h40 (2h40 em Brasília), a polícia foi alertada... de que um aluno do sétimo ano de uma escola em Bistrita teria supostamente atacado uma professora e outro aluno com uma faca”, informou a polícia em comunicado.
Uma fonte judicial disse à Reuters que o adolescente de 13 anos estava sendo investigado sob suspeita de tentativa de homicídio qualificado, mas, por ser menor de idade, não será julgado. A Reuters não conseguiu entrar em contato com o advogado do menino.
A fonte disse que o menino havia postado mensagens no TikTok nas quais ele incitava à violência, mas afirmou que os promotores precisavam examinar seus dispositivos digitais antes de chegar a conclusões.
Não houve comentário imediato do TikTok sobre o caso.
Vários veículos de mídia locais noticiaram que o menino havia postado online sobre suas intenções pouco antes do ataque.
Uma imagem de rede social publicada na mídia local mostrava um menino se fotografando no espelho do banheiro com uma faca e um capacete com uma câmera. Outra mostrava sua mão fazendo o sinal de “OK”. Abaixo, uma mensagem em inglês dizia: “É isso aí, rapazes. Venho preparando isso há 8 meses, vejo vocês no Valhalla”.
A Reuters não conseguiu verificar de forma independente a autenticidade das publicações.
Seu conteúdo era semelhante ao postado por um agressor que matou um zelador de escola no leste da Polônia no início deste mês.
“As notícias da imprensa de que o estudante anunciou seu ataque no TikTok devem ser esclarecidas pelos investigadores”, escreveu o ministro da Educação, Mihai Dimian, no Facebook.

items.title: Brasil registra foco de Doença de Newcastle em perus em Santa Catarina
items.author: Victor Borges
items.creator: Victor Borges
items.summary: O Ministério da Agricultura registrou um foco de Doença de Newcastle em uma criação de perus em Santa Catarina, disse nesta segunda-feira o ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, acrescentando que 133 granjas da região serão afetadas por medidas sanitárias.
items.body:
O Ministério da Agricultura registrou um foco de Doença de Newcastle em uma criação de perus em Santa Catarina, disse nesta segunda-feira o ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, acrescentando que 133 granjas da região serão afetadas por medidas sanitárias.
Autoridades disseram ainda que o ministério está informando parceiros comerciais sobre o caso da doença viral altamente contagiosa para aves, que pode resultar em embargos comerciais às exportações do Brasil, o maior exportador global de carne de frango.
A China, um dos principais destinos das exportações brasileiras de carne de frango, impôs em 2024 um embargo à carne de frango brasileira após a confirmação de um caso de Doença de Newcastle em uma granja comercial no Rio Grande do Sul. Outros países também chegaram a banir provisoriamente o produto brasileiro.
Mas as autoridades acrescentaram que o ministério ainda não recebeu qualquer informação sobre suspensão das exportações brasileiras por conta do foco em perus, em um estabelecimento de avicultura comercial de corte no município de Nova Itaberaba.
"Ainda não temos nada objetivo a informar (sobre suspensão de exportações)", afirmou o secretário-substituto de Comércio e Relações Internacionais do ministério, Rafael Requião.
Ele disse ainda que o Brasil está analisando os protocolos para identificar quais medidas serão tomadas para um eventual "autoembargo" de exportações.
"Não queremos antecipar a reação de parceiros, as discussões com a China começam agora", disse Requião.
Não estava imediatamente claro se eventuais embargos poderiam atingir exportações de carne de peru ou de frango também.
Requião disse ainda que o governo tem trabalhado com protocolos sanitários que permitem a "regionalização" do problema, o que evitaria embargos mais abrangentes sobre a carne brasileira.
O ministro disse que nenhuma ave saiu da granja com registro da doença desde que as investigações começaram.
As medidas de controle, contenção e erradicação do foco serão executadas conforme as diretrizes do Plano de Contingência para Influenza Aviária e Doença de Newcastle, disse o ministério.
O estabelecimento Nova Itaberaba foi interditado pelo Serviço Veterinário Oficial, com suspensão da movimentação de aves.
Já o secretário de Defesa Agropecuária substituto, Allan Alvarenga, afirmou que a doença não representa riscos à população. Ele acrescentou que a Organização Mundial de Saúde Animal foi notificada do caso no domingo.
Apesar da necessidade de adoção de "medidas sanitárias para controlar a ocorrência, o consumo de produtos avícolas submetidos à inspeção oficial permanece seguro, sem contraindicações", ressaltou o ministério, em nota.
Associações de produtores, como ABPA, ACAV e Sindicarne, destacaram em nota que a ocorrência de Doença de Newcastle não apresentou "manifestação clínica". Ou seja, houve a detecção do vírus, mas não da doença nos animais confinados.

items.title: Anthropic monta fundo "de benefício público” e Musk promete doar ações a crianças dos EUA
items.author: Abu Sultan, Deborah Sophia
items.creator: Abu Sultan, Deborah Sophia
items.summary: A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do chatbot Claude, anunciou no domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público para facilitar doações em prol do “bem comum”, enquanto Elon Musk se comprometeu a doar uma ação da SpaceX a “cada criança nos Estados Unidos”.
items.body:
A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do chatbot Claude, anunciou no domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público para facilitar doações em prol do “bem comum”, enquanto Elon Musk se comprometeu a doar uma ação da SpaceX a “cada criança nos Estados Unidos”.
A Anthropic informou que o fundo será constituído como uma sociedade de responsabilidade limitada de propriedade integral e receberá 2% adicionais das ações da companhia, a critério do conselho de administração, para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base que ainda não foi divulgada.
A decisão dará à empresa mais flexibilidade e escala para fazer doações em benefício da humanidade, afirmou a companhia. A empresa está planejando uma das maiores ofertas públicas iniciais (IPOs) de ações da história como uma corporação de benefício público, uma estrutura jurídica que exige que a administração equilibre interesses públicos mais amplos com metas de lucratividade.
Musk respondeu a uma publicação da Anthropic na rede social anunciando o fundo, dizendo que recomenda “doar as ações diretamente ao público”.
“No ano que vem, darei uma das minhas ações da SpaceX para cada criança nos Estados Unidos. Essa será a primeira de muitas”, disse Musk, que dirige a SpaceXSI, rival da Anthropic, nesta segunda-feira. O bilionário detinha cerca de 6,42 bilhões de ações da empresa em junho.
As ações da SpaceX (SPCX.O) subiram 2,5% no início do pregão desta segunda-feira.
Dados do censo dos EUA mostram que há 72 milhões de crianças nos Estados Unidos; se uma única ação da SpaceX fosse distribuída a cada uma delas ao preço atual de negociação de US$149 cada, isso equivaleria a mais de US$10,7 bilhões.
IMPACTO NO TRABALHO A Anthropic, que se posiciona como uma empresa de IA que prioriza a segurança, afirmou que a IA poderá representar “riscos catastróficos ou existenciais para a humanidade” e dedicou cerca de 80 páginas do corpo principal de seu prospecto de IPO, que tem 261 páginas, à exposição dos fatores de risco.
A empresa afirmou em seu blog que o Fundo de Benefício Público poderá apoiar iniciativas que incluem doações para organizações sem fins lucrativos, distribuições diretas a populações específicas e esforços para lidar com o impacto da IA no mercado de trabalho.
A Anthropic está se preparando para uma estreia na bolsa que poderá avaliá-la em cerca de US$2 trilhões, embora a Reuters tenha noticiado com exclusividade na semana passada que alguns investidores estejam considerando uma avaliação menor, de cerca de US$1,5 trilhão. Isso dará à participação de 5% no fundo um valor entre US$75 bilhões e US$100 bilhões.
A Anthropic citou o impacto potencial da IA sobre os trabalhadores como uma das áreas de foco do novo fundo, com base em um compromisso de US$200 milhões anunciado anteriormente para estudar e lidar com as mudanças no mercado de trabalho.
Uma pesquisa do FMI mostra que cerca de 40% dos empregos serão aprimorados, rebaixados ou eliminados pela IA, com esse número chegando a 60% nas economias avançadas, afirmou a diretora-geral Kristalina Georgieva na semana passada.
DOAÇÕES POLÍTICAS? A Anthropic afirmou que nenhuma participação acionária detida por seu fundo será utilizada para lobby ou doações políticas nos EUA ou no exterior.
Somado ao compromisso dos cofundadores de doar 80% de suas participações acionárias e a um programa de contrapartida de doações dos funcionários, cerca de 20% das ações da Anthropic serão destinadas a fins públicos, excluindo quaisquer ações adicionais que venham a ser incorporadas posteriormente.
A Anthropic informou que divulgará mais detalhes nos próximos meses sobre a governança do fundo, sua estrutura e os limites de avaliação que poderiam ampliar sua participação. A empresa também planeja publicar um relatório detalhando o progresso em direção à sua missão.
items.raw_description: A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do chatbot Claude, anunciou no domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público para facilitar doações em prol do “bem comum”, enquanto Elon Musk se comprometeu a doar uma ação da SpaceX a “cada criança nos Estados Unidos”.

items.title: Mulher afirma em tribunal do Reino Unido que comediante Russell Brand a estuprou
items.author: Michael Holden
items.creator: Michael Holden
items.summary: Uma mulher relatou à polícia que o ator e comediante britânico Russell Brand teria agarrado seus seios antes de arrastá-la para um banheiro de um bar e praticar estupro oral nela, segundo depoimento exibido em um tribunal de Londres nesta segunda-feira.
items.body:
Uma mulher relatou à polícia que o ator e comediante britânico Russell Brand teria agarrado seus seios antes de arrastá-la para um banheiro de um bar e praticar estupro oral nela, segundo depoimento exibido em um tribunal de Londres nesta segunda-feira.
Brand, que já foi um dos apresentadores de maior destaque do Reino Unido e é ex-marido da cantora norte-americana Katy Perry, está sendo julgado sob acusação de três crimes de estupro, três de agressão sexual e um de agressão indecente contra seis mulheres entre 1999 e 2009.
O homem de 51 anos nega as acusações e disse à polícia, após sua prisão, que nunca se envolveu em atividade sexual não consensual e que as denunciantes poderiam ter reimaginado os acontecimentos.
A terceira das seis denunciantes a prestar depoimento alegou que Brand a havia agredido depois que ela o conheceu em uma festa em um bar de Londres, em 2004.
“BRAND TINHA UM SORRISO ESTRANHO” Em um depoimento à polícia, dado em lágrimas e exibido aos jurados no Tribunal da Coroa de Southwark, a mulher, que trabalhava para a MTV, disse que queria conhecer Brand porque o tinha visto na televisão e achava que ele era muito engraçado. Mas, menos de um minuto depois de conversar com ele no bar, segundo ela, ele a agrediu.
“Ele literalmente agarrou meus seios no meio da conversa”, disse ela, acrescentando que ele tinha um sorriso estranho e maníaco no rosto enquanto fazia isso.
Imediatamente depois, enquanto ela estava em choque e sem acreditar no que estava acontecendo, ela disse que ele agarrou seu braço e a puxou para os banheiros que ficavam nas proximidades. Foi lá que ele supostamente a estuprou oralmente.
“Aconteceu tão rápido”, ela contou à polícia. “Ele disse ‘vamos lá, vamos lá, não seja desmancha-prazeres’”, ela relatou, dizendo que ele a segurava à força pela cabeça e pelos cabelos. “Eu simplesmente congelei. Não sabia o que fazer.”
Ela disse que, embora as palavras dele não fossem ameaçadoras, a força do ataque e o olhar dele sim.
Ela rejeitou a sugestão do advogado de Brand, Ian Winter, de que ela teria ficado muito animada ao conhecê-lo, dizendo que “não estava impressionada com a celebridade... Eu não era uma colegial boba”.
Winter argumentou que, se ela tivesse sido apalpada no bar ou arrastada para o banheiro, as pessoas teriam visto.
“Vamos deixar claro que ele não fez isso com você”, disse ele sobre a suposta agressão sexual. “Você acompanhou alegremente o Sr. Brand até o banheiro”, acrescentou ele, sugestão que ela rejeitou.
Ele afirmou que o suposto incidente no banheiro era “fisicamente impossível e não aconteceu”.
Winter também questionou por que ela nunca havia dito que havia sido estuprada até depois de um documentário de 2023 e de uma reportagem na imprensa sobre Brand, tendo contado a amigos e à irmã que ele havia tentado se impor a ela, mas que ela havia conseguido fugir.
“Eu não queria que as pessoas me julgassem... Eu sentia vergonha”, disse ela.
Na semana passada, a primeira denunciante disse ao tribunal que Brand a havia estuprado depois que ela o conheceu em um evento paralelo à conferência do Partido Trabalhista de 1999, no sul da Inglaterra.
A segunda das denunciantes contou ao Tribunal da Coroa de Southwark, em Londres, que, em 2001, um Brand com “olhos descontrolados” tentou arrastá-la para o banheiro masculino da MTV Europe, em Londres, onde ela trabalhava.
O julgamento, que deve durar cerca de seis semanas, continua.

items.title: Pensión IVSS de noviembre de 2026 en Venezuela: fecha de pago y monto por Patria
items.author: Raylí Luján
items.summary: El calendario de pagos mantiene la práctica de adelantar la pensión al mes anterior al que corresponde.
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — Los pensionados del Instituto Venezolano de los Seguros Sociales (IVSS) en Venezuela están a la espera del pago correspondiente a noviembre de 2026, que podría acreditarse esta semana, de acuerdo con las previsiones difundidas por medios locales. Sin embargo, hasta el momento, la fecha debe considerarse estimada y no una confirmación oficial del organismo. El calendario de pagos mantiene la práctica de adelantar la pensión al mes anterior al que corresponde. De cumplirse esta previsión, los beneficiarios recibirían en octubre el abono correspondiente a noviembre, mientras esperan también la asignación complementaria que el Gobierno distribuye a través del Sistema Patria. Ver más: Saime: requisitos y pasos para renovar cédulas sin cita este 2026 La fecha prevista para el depósito de la pensión del IVSS de noviembre es el miércoles 21 de octubre de 2026. La estimación sigue el patrón de los últimos meses, cuando el organismo ha efectuado los pagos alrededor del día 21. El pasado 21 de septiembre, por ejemplo, el IVSS informó sobre el depósito correspondiente a octubre. El pago de la pensión se deposita en la cuenta bancaria registrada por el beneficiario. Este abono es distinto de las asignaciones complementarias que se distribuyen mediante la plataforma Patria, cuyos cronogramas y montos pueden anunciarse por separado. La pensión mensual del IVSS permanece en 130 bolívares, una cantidad que no ha cambiado desde marzo de 2022. A la tasa oficial de cambio, su equivalente en dólares es mínimo y no representa una fuente de ingresos suficiente para cubrir los gastos básicos de una persona mayor. Por separado, los pensionados reciben un ingreso complementario que el Gobierno canaliza mediante el Sistema Patria. En los anuncios de 2026, este beneficio se ha identificado como Ingreso Integral y anteriormente se conocía como Bono contra la Guerra Económica. Para los pensionados y jubilados, el Ejecutivo anunció en abril un ingreso complementario de referencia de US$70 mensuales. La conversión a bolívares depende de la tasa oficial del Banco Central de Venezuela (BCV) aplicable al momento del pago. Por ello, las cifras difundidas en redes sociales o portales informativos sobre un posible depósito de 61.390 bolívares deben tratarse como estimaciones y no como un monto confirmado para noviembre. Los beneficiarios pueden comprobar si la pensión fue acreditada mediante la banca electrónica de la entidad financiera en la que reciben habitualmente el depósito. Para verificar el ingreso complementario, pueden ingresar en el portal oficial del Sistema Patria y revisar el monedero y el historial de asignaciones. El procedimiento recomendado es: La distribución de los beneficios puede ser progresiva, por lo que no todos los beneficiarios necesariamente reciben la asignación el mismo día. Tampoco es necesario activar un bono mediante intermediarios ni compartir claves bancarias o contraseñas para recibirlo. La diferencia entre la pensión base y el ingreso complementario refleja el peso que han adquirido las bonificaciones en la política de remuneraciones del Estado venezolano. Aunque estos pagos adicionales elevan el ingreso nominal de los beneficiarios, no modifican el monto legal de la pensión del seguro social. Ver más: IVSS: Venezuela confirmó el monto del bono de pensión de septiembre 2026 La pensión de 130 bolívares continúa congelada desde marzo de 2022, mientras que las asignaciones complementarias se gestionan mediante mecanismos separados. Esta estructura hace que el ingreso total dependa de los anuncios y desembolsos periódicos del Ejecutivo, además de la evolución del tipo de cambio y de los precios.

items.title: Eagles quarterback Hurts set to miss rest of season due to blood clots
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent said on Monday, and media reports said the former Super Bowl MVP was expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season.
items.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent said on Monday, and media reports said the former Super Bowl MVP was expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season.
The Eagles announced on Thursday that Hurts had a superficial blood clot in his calf. Medical experts have evaluated him over the past few days.
"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli," the Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn said in a statement.
The Eagles played in London on October 11, losing 19-17 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
A bilateral pulmonary embolism is where a blood clot travels from a deep vein in the body, often the leg, and blocks an artery in both lungs.
Hurts guided the Eagles to the Super Bowl title in February 2025, throwing for two touchdowns and running in another against the Kansas City Chiefs to earn the game's Most Valuable Player trophy.
He is clinically stable and his treatment should only involve blood thinners, which will rule him out of contact activities, the statement said.
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners," the statement said, adding no long-term effects are expected.

items.title: Russian attack kills six at park in Kharkiv region, including three children, Ukraine says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A Russian drone attack on Monday killed six people, including three children, in a park in a village in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
items.body:
A Russian drone attack on Monday killed six people, including three children, in a park in a village in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
Syniehubov, writing on Telegram, had earlier said 15 people were injured in the strike southwest of the city of Kharkiv.
The drone hit a park where families were playing with children, Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said.
Vyhivskyi shared a blurred photo showing a child's body in a stroller. Other pictures posted online showed emergency crews working around a damaged building.

items.summary: Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested this weekend on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants, according to ABC affiliate KATU of Portland, Ore.
items.body:
Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested this weekend on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants, according to ABC affiliate KATU of Portland, Ore.
According to the report, Stewart was booked by police in Springfield, Ore., early Sunday morning and later released.
He leads the Ducks in receptions (27) and receiving yards (352) and is tied for the team lead with four touchdown catches.
The school had not commented on the matter as of Monday morning.
A senior from Memphis, Tenn., Stewart did not play in Saturday's 17-14 home win against Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury.
The Ducks (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) return to action this Saturday on the road against Illinois (3-3, 1-2).
Stewart has 166 catches for 2,128 yards and 15 touchdowns in 36 career games with Texas A&M (2022-23) and Oregon (2024, 2026). He missed the entire 2025 season with a torn patellar tendon.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Canadian firms' outlooks dimmed after trade talks collapse, BoC survey finds
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Promit Mukherjee and David Ljunggren
items.body:
By Promit Mukherjee and David Ljunggren
OTTAWA, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Canadian firms reported their outlooks had deteriorated after the collapse of trade talks with the United States but sentiments remained considerably stronger than at the peak of tensions last year, the Bank of Canada said on Monday.
A survey of around 340 business leaders in September showed that since the talks broke down on August 21, new US tariffs and Canadian counter tariffs had weighed on their outlooks.
The bank said this suggested "a moderation rather than a fundamental shift in firms' outlooks".
A separate Business Outlook Survey for the third quarter, which was largely carried out before the talks collapsed, showed overall sentiment had improved.
But both surveys pointed to higher inflation expectations amid increase input costs and elevated selling prices due to trade tensions and the Middle East crisis.
The studies help the BoC decide the trajectory of inflation and feed into its decision for the monetary policy.
Money markets are pricing in a hold in interest rates by the BoC on October 28, but see a 25 basis point rise in December.
Governor Tiff Macklem says while headline inflation has risen, this is primarily due by higher energy costs and there are so far no signs of a spillover into other components.
But he also says he is ready to hike rates if higher prices show signs of feeding into the broader economy.
The leaders' survey reported weaker export sales, the BoC said, adding that the improving sentiment at the beginning of the third quarter had partially reversed.
"Nevertheless, sentiment and expectations remain considerably stronger than at the height of trade tensions in 2025," it added.
In the Business Outlook Survey, the central bank said while there were some improvements in demand, firms' hiring intentions remained soft, but most firms intend to retain existing employees. Expectations for wage growth are largely unchanged, the survey noted.
The business outlook indicator, a metric of prospects under current economic conditions, edged up to -0.33 in the third quarter from -0.38 in the prior three months.
A separate survey by the central bank on consumer expectations showed that more than 50% of consumers surveyed expect a recession over the next 12 months and expectations for five-year inflation had also risen.
((Reuters Ottawa bureau))
Keywords: CANADA CENBANK/

items.title: Israel to resume commercial shipments to Gaza after Hamas fee dispute
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Israel said on Monday it would resume allowing commercial goods shipments into Gaza after a days-long halt over a tax dispute involving Hamas and merchants, restoring a key route for food and other essentials to the aid-dependent enclave.
items.body:
Israel said on Monday it would resume allowing commercial goods shipments into Gaza after a days-long halt over a tax dispute involving Hamas and merchants, restoring a key route for food and other essentials to the aid-dependent enclave.
COGAT, the Israeli military agency overseeing humanitarian affairs in Gaza, said it made the decision after [USN:L8N4611UU TEXT:"merchants"] reported that Hamas authorities had withdrawn demands for payments of 10,000 shekels ($3,225) per truck.
"The resumption of coordination is being carried out in accordance with Israel's commitment to the humanitarian provisions of the ceasefire agreement," it said.
COGAT said the merchants' accounts had not been independently verified and shipments would resume gradually, with priority given to essential goods ahead of winter.
Oversight would be tightened to ensure payments are made and received only through documented bank transfers, with any merchant found to have paid Hamas facing exclusion from the system.
Hamas said the 10,000-shekel fee was a voluntary contribution by better-off Gazans to a national fund supporting people in need in the war-ravaged territory.
Most Gazans remain dependent on aid after three years of war, repeated displacement and severe restrictions on aid deliveries . While last year's US-brokered ceasefire halted the heaviest fighting, it has not ended Israeli attacks.
Local health officials said on Monday that at least five Palestinians, including a 14-year-old boy, were killed in separate Israeli strikes in Gaza City and Khan Younis. The Israeli military did not immediately comment.
Israel says Hamas has continued to rearm and carry out attacks in violation of the ceasefire, while Hamas accuses Israel of undermining the agreement.
Gaza health officials say about 1,500 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the October 2025 ceasefire, while Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.
($1 = 3.0991 shekels)

items.title: Egypt delays vote on military support for Saudi Arabia until October 26
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Egypt's parliament delayed until October 26 a vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, extending deliberations over a potentially deeper Egyptian role in the conflict with Yemen's Houthis.
items.body:
Egypt's parliament delayed until October 26 a vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, extending deliberations over a potentially deeper Egyptian role in the conflict with Yemen's Houthis.
Members of the House of Representatives said it adjourned a second closed-door session on Monday, held to discuss President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request for authority to take measures [USN:L6N46403J TEXT:"to support the kingdom"] following recent attacks.
Egypt's constitution requires a two-thirds parliamentary majority to approve sending its armed forces on a combat mission beyond the country's borders, after consultation with the National Defence Council.
Sisi said on [USN:L1N46401H TEXT:"Saturday"] that Egypt would take "any measure" necessary to protect Gulf allies, marking a sharper public commitment after Houthi attacks on Saudi oil and other infrastructure.
The Egyptian Social Democratic Party said on Sunday it had instructed its lawmakers to abstain, saying parliament had not received sufficient information about the proposed mission's objectives, scope, duration, cost or risks to Egyptian troops.
While affirming support for Saudi security, the party said Egypt should avoid an open-ended military commitment and preserve room for diplomacy, citing the country's economic pressures and the risks to Red Sea shipping and Suez Canal revenue.
Al-Azhar's grand imam also called on Sunday for an urgent mediation effort by Arab and Muslim leaders to contain the conflict and avert further bloodshed.
The issue underscores Cairo's close security and financial ties with Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has a $5.3 billion deposit at Egypt's central bank due this month, plus $267.39 million in interest, central bank data showed.
Egypt's EGX30 index, which fell early in the session amid concern over possible military involvement, recovered to close 0.4% higher.
Nematallah Choucri, head of research at HC Securities, said geopolitical developments had become the main factor behind recent market losses.

items.title: Reports: Falcons signing Andy Dalton, cutting Cooper Rush
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are signing veteran Andy Dalton and releasing fellow quarterback Cooper Rush, according to multiple media reports Monday.
items.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are signing veteran Andy Dalton and releasing fellow quarterback Cooper Rush, according to multiple media reports Monday.
Dalton, who turns 39 on Oct. 29, was released by the Philadelphia Eagles on Oct. 9 after throwing an interception on his only pass attempt of the season in a Week 3 loss at Chicago.
Since playing his first nine seasons and making three Pro Bowls with the Cincinnati Bengals from 2011-19, Dalton has played for the Dallas Cowboys, Bears, New Orleans Saints, Carolina Panthers and Eagles.
Rush started the Falcons' first two games this season as Michael Penix Jr. completed his recovery from ACL surgery, losing to the Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers.
Atlanta (2-4) also has veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and undrafted rookie Jack Strand on the roster.
Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards with 254 touchdowns and 152 interceptions across 180 career games, compiling a record of 84-83-2 as a starter in the regular season.
Rush, 32, completed 22 of 39 passes for 229 yards with one TD and four picks this season. He was a longtime backup with the Dallas Cowboys before making two starts last season for the Baltimore Ravens.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Second-hand clothing app Vinted purges suspected stolen goods after France riots
items.author: Anna Peverieri
items.creator: Anna Peverieri
items.summary: Vinted, an app for buying and selling second-hand clothing, said on Monday it had increased checks on suspicious listings and removed adverts linked to looted goods following unrest in France.
items.body:
Vinted, an app for buying and selling second-hand clothing, said on Monday it had increased checks on suspicious listings and removed adverts linked to looted goods following unrest in France.
Nationwide demonstrations across France over the cost of living and declining public service [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"deteriorated into riots"] on Saturday, with shops looted across the country as violent groups clashed with police in one of the worst days of violence in years.
Vinted said its teams had taken "immediate action" since the weekend to identify and remove listings suspected of being linked to looting, and had increased scrutiny of suspicious adverts.
Accounts found to have breached its rules could face permanent bans, it said.
"The sale of stolen goods, or soliciting them, is strictly prohibited on Vinted, and we have zero tolerance for it," a Vinted spokesperson said in a statement.
The company said it was working with law enforcement and French authorities and would continue to adapt its processes to identify and counter emerging risks and malicious behaviour.
Serge Papin, France's small businesses minister, said on X that authorities would meet later in the day with marketplace operators and officials from the interior and justice ministries, after goods stolen during Saturday's unrest were offered for sale online.
Platforms including Vinted, Amazon, eBay and TikTok were invited to the meeting on Monday, according to government officials.
Vinted did not say whether it had seen a similar increase in suspicious listings in [USN:L8N46407Z TEXT:"Italy"], where unrest also led to the looting of luxury stores.
France, the UK and Italy are Vinted's largest markets.
[USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"Luxury groups"] including Louis Vuitton (LVMH.PA) and Rolex, as well as make-up retail giant Sephora, have been caught up in unrest in [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"France"] and [USN:L8N46407Z TEXT:"Italy"] where some of the most violent protests seen in decades over living costs and declining public services have prompted police to fire tear gas and use water cannon as demonstrators looted shops and set fires.
Founded in Lithuania in 2008, Vinted became the Baltic state's first "unicorn" - a startup valued at €1 billion - in 2019. A secondary share transaction led by Sweden's EQT Growth [USN:L4N41A19T TEXT:"valued Vinted at €8 billion"] earlier this year.
The online marketplace prohibits the sale of stolen items and relies on reports from retailers and users, among other checks, to detect suspicious listings.
items.raw_description: Vinted, an app for buying and selling second-hand clothing, said on Monday it had increased checks on suspicious listings and removed adverts linked to looted goods following unrest in France.

items.title: UK's Doncaster Sheffield Airport set for public ownership ahead of reopening
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain's Doncaster Sheffield Airport, which closed almost four years ago but handled more than 1.4 million passengers in 2019, looks set to return to public ownership with a view to reopening next year.
items.body:
Britain's Doncaster Sheffield Airport, which closed almost four years ago but handled more than 1.4 million passengers in 2019, looks set to return to public ownership with a view to reopening next year.
South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority on Monday said its mayor and regional leaders were set approve a deal to buy the airport, and adjacent land called the Innovation Quarter, from current owners Peel Land.
• SYMCA plans to restore freight services from autumn 2027 and passenger services from spring 2028, subject to regulatory and operational work needed to reopen the airport
• The deal needs formal approval from the boards of SYMCA and Peel Land
• Last year SYMCA approved about £160 million ($213 million)of funding for the reopening
• SYMCA did not immediately disclose how much it would pay Peel. A report to its board said the deal was "not without risk" to the taxpayer, but recommended approval
• SYMCA would become freehold owner of the site
• The South Yorkshire region, home to Boeing's first European factory, seeks to make the airport area a hub for sustainable aviation and advanced manufacturing
• Peel closed the airport in November 2022, saying it had never made a profit, after Wizz Air pulled its based aircraft. Peel rejected an offer of public money to cover losses for a year
• The reopening has been repeatedly delayed. As recently as February 2025, local authorities were targeting passenger flights by spring 2026
($1 = 0.7512 pounds)

items.title: Rendimientos de bonos Tesoro EEUU suben levemente mientras disminuyen temores sobre la IA
items.author: Chuck Mikolajczak
items.creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
items.summary: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU subían ligeramente el lunes y el retorno de los bonos a 10 años se recuperaba tras su mayor caída semanal en siete meses, mientras se disipaban las preocupaciones sobre el impacto del aumento de las tasas de interés en las acciones del sector de la IA.
items.body:
Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU subían ligeramente el lunes y el retorno de los bonos a 10 años se recuperaba tras su mayor caída semanal en siete meses, mientras se disipaban las preocupaciones sobre el impacto del aumento de las tasas de interés en las acciones del sector de la IA.
* El rendimiento a 10 años cayó 14,6 puntos básicos la semana pasada, incluso tras conocerse unos datos de inflación más altos de lo esperado, reflejados en el índice de precios al consumo y el índice de precios al productor.
* Los mercados bursátiles sufrieron una corrección debido a la preocupación de que las inversiones en acciones de infraestructuras de IA pudieran empezar a agotarse, lo que potenció el atractivo de los bonos del Tesoro como valor refugio.
* Sin embargo, las acciones subían en las primeras horas de negociación del lunes, gracias a la recuperación de los valores relacionados con la IA, mientras que el descenso de los precios del petróleo también contribuía a mitigar los temores inflacionarios.
* El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años subía 0,8 puntos básicos, al 5,106%. El rendimiento del bono a 30 años subía 1,2 puntos básicos, al 5,447%.
* Un segmento muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, que mide la diferencia entre el retorno de la deuda a dos y a diez años —y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas—, se situaba en 35,3 puntos básicos positivos.
* Esta semana llegará más oferta al mercado cuando el Tesoro subaste el miércoles 13.000 millones de dólares en bonos a 20 años y el jueves 26.000 millones de dólares en Títulos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos protegidos contra la inflación (TIPS) a 5 años .
* El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subía 1,3 puntos básicos al 4,749%.
* Las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas al menos 25 puntos básicos en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana se sitúan en el 17,2%, según el CME FedWatch, lo que supone un descenso respecto al 21% de hace una semana y al 57,6% de hace un mes.

items.title: South Africa must prepare for potential loss of US trade benefits, president says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Monday that the country must prepare for its potential exclusion from the United States' duty-free trade initiative, AGOA, as relations between Washington and Pretoria have soured.
items.body:
South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Monday that the country must prepare for its potential exclusion from the United States' duty-free trade initiative, AGOA, as relations between Washington and Pretoria have soured.
The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) gives eligible African countries duty-free access to the US market for thousands of products. South Africa has benefited from it for years.
President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:S0N43F07R TEXT:"cracked down on"] South Africa for what Trump claims is its persecution of white people. South Africa's government says this is a falsehood spread by fringe groups.
Ramaphosa said it remained to be seen whether South Africa would remain part of AGOA and his government was in discussions with US counterparts. Some US officials have suggested [USN:S0N3XA08H TEXT:"South Africa should be excluded"].
"I need, as president, to prepare us if it ever happens," Ramaphosa said. He said the impact on jobs would be "devastating" and he and Deputy President Paul Mashatile have been travelling around the world to explore alternative markets.
Ramaphosa cited a recent trade agreement with China as a positive step. China introduced a zero-tariff scheme for qualifying South African goods in May.

items.title: Carney says cause of fire at Alberta military base still unknown
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday that the cause of a firethat killed at least four military members and injured dozens of others in Alberta on Saturday is still unknown.
items.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday that the cause of a fire that killed at least four military members and injured dozens of others in Alberta on Saturday is still unknown.
Carney said in an address to Parliament that soldiers and reserve members were conducting live-fire exercises at an army base in Wainwright while a fire was burning in the training area.
“Driven by ferocious winds, the fire jumped nearly a kilometer in less than a minute to where soldiers were gathered,” Carney said. He added that 50 investigators are currently on the ground, from the army and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, to determine how the disaster happened.
"This loss touches every corner of the nation," Carney said.
Officials said 39 people remain hospitalized, with 19 people in critical condition. The soldiers and reserve members were preparing to deploy to Latvia, where Canadian forces have their largest international military operation.
Kent Moore, a professor of atmospheric physics at the University of Toronto, said the embers from grass fires in dry conditions can spread incredibly quickly. He said there didn't appear to be any rain in the area, so it was unlikely the fire was triggered by lightning.
"The fact that the winds were so strong suggests to me that it wouldn't have taken much to start this fire," he said, speculating that it was likely caused by human error, including sparks from vehicles or live fire, or an errant cigarette from a smoker.
