LONDON, Oct 19 : Britain risks becoming a "high-value AI customer" rather than a country able to shape the technology unless it takes urgent action to build domestic capabilities, the government's top science advisers said on Monday.
Governments around the world are racing to build AI capabilities, driven by concerns that countries without their own expertise, computing infrastructure and models could become increasingly dependent on a handful of mostly U.S.-based companies that dominate the technology.
The Council for Science and Technology, an independent advisory body that advises the government on science and technology policy, said decisions made now would determine whether Britain captures the economic and public benefits of AI while maintaining resilience and strategic autonomy.
"The way for us to achieve AI sovereignty is to build trusted systems that deliver real public, economic and security benefits," the advisers said in an emailed letter to the AI minister, Kanishka Narayan.

The council warned that Britain was at risk of falling behind and becoming a "high-value AI customer, rather than a country able to shape the technology and its usage," without what it described as "deliberate and urgent action."
It recommended appointing a single government lead to coordinate AI sovereignty policy, investing in skills, data and computing infrastructure, and testing AI systems in areas including national security, health and education.
The advisers also said Britain should maintain access to the world's most advanced AI systems while developing some domestic capabilities of its own, including exploring a publicly governed British AI model that could be made available to researchers, startups and public services.
The government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Source: Reuters

items.title: France's unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months
items.author: Michel Rose
items.creator: Michel Rose
items.summary: France’s worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office deeper into turmoil, exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order.
items.body:
France’s worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office deeper into [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"turmoil"], exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order.
The [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"rioting"] that swept across France on Saturday, leaving a trail of looted shops, torched buildings and defaced public institutions, presents Macron with perhaps the most explosive challenge of his twilight presidency: a country demanding more from a state that can no longer afford to give much.
Macron came to power almost a decade ago promising to upend France’s sclerotic political class, turbocharge economic reforms and restore authority through a more assertive presidency. Instead, with just six months left in office, he finds himself effectively a lame-duck head of state presiding over a country mired in political paralysis, facing acute [USN:L6N46502R TEXT:"financial pressures"] and grappling with unrest that has exposed the limits of state authority.
Unlike during the Yellow Vest uprising of 2018-2019, when Macron sought to defuse public anger with billions of euros in concessions, France’s strained public finances and fractured parliament leave him with precious few levers to pull.
Even former allies are now openly scathing, tracing the country's current impasse to Macron's decision to call a [USN:L8N3J00J1 TEXT:"snap parliamentary election"] in 2024 that weakened his authority.
“The end of this term is a slow agony,” said Loïc Kervran, a former lawmaker from Macron’s camp, on X. “The president paralysed the country with his absurd decision to dissolve parliament in 2024. Arguably the worst decision in the history of the Fifth Republic."
LE PEN'S 'HIGHWAY' TO THE PRESIDENCY The turmoil may benefit far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, who is already the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race and stands to gain from both the anger over declining living standards and the fears over law and order unleashed by the weekend’s violence.
"Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, another former Macron lawmaker, told Reuters. "It's not just a clear path ahead of her — it's a six-lane highway."
Le Pen delivered her own message to the nation in a video statement on Sunday, portraying Macron's administration as a crumbling power and casting herself as the figure capable of restoring order.
When Macron later addressed the country, he offered little concrete action, stopping short of declaring a state of emergency. As he spoke, looting was continuing for a second consecutive night, including in affluent Paris districts, prompting his prime minister Sébastien Lecornu to announce local curfews on Monday.
Opponents and one-time allies alike were underwhelmed. His former prime minister, Edouard Philippe, now preparing his own presidential run, was unsparing in his criticism.
"Mr President, I listened to you last night," he wrote on X. "I would have preferred, like millions of French people, decisions and initiatives to restore order."
"Our country needs to be commanded," he added.
But even Philippe is struggling to shake off his past association with Macron, and most recent polls show far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon edging ahead of him in the race to qualify for the second-round runoff vote. That outcome would all but guarantee a Le Pen victory, according to opinion polls.
CALLS FOR EARLY RESIGNATION AMID MULTIPLE CRISES Macron's office on Monday announced that he had refused his interior minister's resignation and ordered a review into apparent failures in intelligence gathering and police preparedness — deepening the impression of a government struggling to regain control.
[USN:L1N465097 TEXT:"Investors also took fright"]. Market analysts say the violence adds another layer of political risk at a time when France is already under scrutiny over its swelling debt burden and struggle to reduce one of the euro zone's largest budget deficits.
The president now finds himself trapped between bond markets demanding spending restraint and protesters demanding the opposite.
Despite calls from opponents to remain in France, Macron arrived in Kuwait on Monday on a Gulf tour he says will help secure fuel supplies and ease some of the economic pressures that have helped swell the ranks of the protesters.
The trip carries risks, reinforcing perceptions of a president disconnected from the public mood. Images of Macron attending a Céline Dion concert with his wife Brigitte on Friday evening, hours before the unrest erupted, prompted ridicule on social media and became an easy symbol for critics seeking to portray him as detached from events.
In a sign of the depth of disenchantment in parts of his political camp, some former allies have begun openly discussing whether he should leave office before the end of his term. Moreau, who spoke to Macron on Sunday, said he urged him to prepare an orderly early departure to break the current political deadlock and avoid another six months of drift.
"He doesn't want to give up, that's not his character. But that's what he should do for the country," he said.

items.title: Suède-La dirigeante du Parti du Centre va étudier la possibilité de former un gouvernement
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président du Parlement suédois a déclaré lundi avoir demandé à la dirigeante du Parti du Centre, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, d'étudier les possibilités de formation d'un nouveau gouvernement, lui accordant une semaine pour rencontrer les autres partis.
items.body:
Le président du Parlement suédois a déclaré lundi avoir demandé à la dirigeante du Parti du Centre, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, d'étudier les possibilités de formation d'un nouveau gouvernement, lui accordant une semaine pour rencontrer les autres partis.
[USN:L8N45600R TEXT:"Les élections du mois dernier"] ont donné au centre-gauche une courte majorité au Parlement, mais si les quatre partis le constituant, dont le Parti du Centre, soutiennent l'accession de la cheffe de file des sociaux-démocrates, Magdalena Andersson, au poste de Première ministre, ils ne s'accordent pas sur la composition du nouveau gouvernement.
Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist va désormais étudier une alternative centriste, a déclaré le président du Riksdag, Andreas Norlen, lors d'une conférence de presse, ajoutant qu’il n’était pas certain de savoir qui deviendrait Premier ministre en cas de succès des discussions.
"Différentes options gouvernementales sont également à l’étude, mais aucune ne semble progresser clairement, pour autant que je puisse en juger", a déclaré Andreas Norlen.
Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, dont le parti est arrivé en cinquième position lors des élections du mois dernier, a déclaré qu'elle inviterait tous les chefs de parti à des discussions.
"Mon ambition est de contribuer à trouver une solution à la question de la formation du gouvernement et non de devenir moi-même Première ministre", a-t-elle ajouté dans un message publié sur la plate-forme X.
[USN:L8N45K0DO TEXT:"Les députés"] ont rejeté jeudi, comme largement attendu, la proposition de Magdalena Andersson de former un gouvernement minoritaire, lors du premier des quatre votes au maximum avant la convocation obligatoire de nouvelles élections. La Suède n’a pas organisé d'élections anticipées depuis 1958.

items.title: ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求　市場改革も表明
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - インドネシア株式市場は１９日、２営業日の下落としては過去最大を記録した。指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩが１６日、２０２７年に同国を「新興国市場」から除外する可能性を警告したことが売りを誘発。当局はＭＳＣＩに説明を求めた。

ジャカルタ総合指数は１６日に１１．６％急落したのに続き、１９日は３．６％安で取引を終えた。２営業日の下落率は１９９８年のアジア金融危機時を含め過去最大となった。取引時間中には６年ぶりの安値も付けた。

ＭＳＣＩが１６日、インドネシアを「新興国市場」から「スタンドアローン市場」に変更することを検討していると表明したことで売りが始まった。想定以上に厳しい分類変更の可能性に、投資家や当局者に動揺が広がった。

スタンドアローン市場に変更されれば、東南アジア最大の経済規模を持つインドネシアは国際資本へのアクセスを失い、投資先として周縁に追いやられる恐れがある。

不安心理からの売りは通貨や債券市場にも波及した。ルピアは１ドル＝１万８０３０ルピアに下落、６月に付けた過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに迫った。国債も下落し、１０年債利回りは１６日の７．１６９％から７．４％に上昇した。

インドネシア証券取引所のジェフリー・ヘンドリック最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、説明を求めるためのＭＳＣＩとの会合を前に「（ＭＳＣＩから）このような発表があるとは予想していなかった。予想外の声明で市場はパニックに陥った」と述べた。

＜資本市場改革への取り組み継続＞

ヘンドリック氏はＭＳＣＩとのオンライン会合後、１月にＭＳＣＩが最初の警告を発したことを受けて着手した資本市場改革に引き続き取り組むと述べた。会合の詳細は明らかにできないとした。

同氏はまた、市場の透明性と価格発見機能を改善するための２つの施策を発表した。同一の個人や法人に株式保有が高度に集中している銘柄をジャカルタ総合指数から除外する措置が含まれる。「主要指数の動きをより正確に示す」ことが狙いという。

インドネシア証券取引所（ＩＤＸ）は１９日、価格変動の抑制に向け、株価の１日の下落率の上限を１５％から７％に縮小した。それを下回る価格での売り注文を自動的に拒否し、一段の下落を防ぐ。

＜投資家、インドネシア資産への投資を再評価＞

ＭＳＣＩの動きを受け、投資家がインドネシア資産全般への投資を見直す中、規制当局や財政・金融当局への圧力が強まっている。

かつて新興国市場の有望な投資先だった同国からの資本逃避リスクへの懸念も高まった。投資家によると、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック以降、プラボウォ大統領の下で財政の健全性や中央銀行の独立性への信頼が薄れる中、同国の魅力は既に低下していた。

事情に詳しい政府当局者２人によると、プラボウォ氏は１９日、財政・金融当局者と会合を開き、「現在の経済情勢」について協議した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・レーティングのソブリン担当アナリスト、レイン・リン氏は、ＭＳＣＩの最新の警告で追加の資本流出が起きる可能性が高いものの、資金調達コストを大幅に押し上げる規模にはならないとの見方を示した。「より懸念されるのは、投資家の信頼が損なわれる可能性と、国債市場や海外直接投資にも投資家心理の悪化が広く波及するリスクだ」と述べた。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＭＳＣＩ指数から完全に除外されれば、パッシブ運用資金が５６億ドル流出する可能性があると推計。これらの指数をベンチマークとするアクティブ運用ファンドの保有額は８０億ドルを超えるものの、売却するかどうかは指数への連動ではなく、運用者の裁量によると記した。

海外投資家は２６年に入り、インドネシア株を４９億８０００万ドル売り越している。年間の資金流出額は少なくとも過去１６年で最大となるペースだ。

items.title: Woman tells UK court that comedian Russell Brand raped her
items.author: Michael Holden
items.creator: Michael Holden
items.summary: A woman told police that British actor and comedian Russell Brand had grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet at a bar and orally raping her, a London court heard on Monday.
items.body:
A woman told police that British actor and comedian [USN:L8N4600OQ TEXT:"Russell Brand"] had grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet at a bar and orally raping her, a London court heard on Monday.
Brand, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters and the former husband of US singer Katy Perry, is [USN:L1N4610E0 TEXT:"on trial accused"] of three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women between 1999 and 2009.
The 51-year-old denies the allegations, and told police after his arrest that he had never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity and the accusers might have re-imagined events.
The third of the six complainants to give evidence alleged Brand had assaulted her after she met him at a party in a London bar in 2004.
BRAND HAD A WEIRD GRIN, WOMAN SAYS In a tearful police interview played to jurors at Southwark Crown Court, the woman, who worked for MTV, said she had wanted to meet Brand because she had seen him on television and thought he was really funny. But less than a minute after talking to him at the bar, she said, he assaulted her.
"He literally just grabbed my boobs in the middle of the conversation," she said, adding that he had a weird, maniacal grin on his face as he did it.
Immediately afterwards while she was in shock and disbelief, she said he grabbed her arm and pulled her to the toilets that were nearby. It was there that he allegedly orally raped her.
"It happened so fast," she told police. "He said 'come on, come on, don't be a spoilsport'," she recounted, saying he was holding her forcibly by her head and hair. "I just froze. I didn't know what to do."
She said while his words were not threatening, the force of the encounter and the look in his eye had been.
She rejected Brand's lawyer Ian Winter's suggestion that she had been very excited to meet him, saying she "wasn't star struck ... I wasn't a giddy schoolgirl".
Winter put it to her that had she been groped at the bar or dragged into the toilets, people would have seen.
"Let's be clear he did not do that to you," he said of the alleged sexual assault. "You happily accompanied Mr Brand into the lavatory," he added, a suggestion she rejected.
He said the alleged incident in the toilet was "physically impossible and it did not happen".
Winter also queried why she had never said she was raped until after a 2023 documentary and press report about Brand, having told friends and her sister he had tried to force himself on her but she had got away.
"I didn't want people to judge me ... I felt ashamed," she said.
Last week, the first complainant told the court that Brand had raped her after she met him at a fringe event at the 1999 Labour Party conference in southern England.
The second of the complainants told London's Southwark Crown Court that in 2001 a "wild-eyed" Brand [USN:L8N46211H TEXT:"had tried to pull her"] into the male toilets at MTV Europe, in London, where she was working.
The trial, which is expected to last around six weeks, continues.
items.raw_description: A woman told police that British actor and comedian Russell Brand had grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet at a bar and orally raping her, a London court heard on Monday.

items.title: Google, McKinsey strike Brazil carbon removal deal with silvopasture project
items.author: Gabriel Araujo
items.creator: Gabriel Araujo
items.summary: Google and McKinsey have agreed to buy 320,000 metric tons of carbon removal credits over 10 years in its first-ever silvopasture project, as part of its commitments through the Symbiosis Coalition, in what is an emerging approach to climate mitigation.
items.body:
Google and McKinsey have agreed to buy 320,000 metric tons of carbon removal credits over 10 years in its first-ever silvopasture project, as part of its commitments through the Symbiosis Coalition, in what is an emerging approach to climate mitigation.
The long-term purchase agreements announced on Monday will support an effort by Working Trees, a climate technology company, to convert degraded cattle pasture into mixed-species systems across Brazil's southeastern [USN:L1N4620RV TEXT:"Amazon and Cerrado"] regions, the coalition said.
Silvopasture integrates trees into cattle pastures, allowing ranching to continue while boosting carbon sequestration and reducing pressure for deforestation.
The deal will help fund the restoration of 8,700 hectares (21,500 acres) of degraded and semi-degraded pastureland as part of a broader 50,000-hectare project and is one of the first attempts to deploy carbon-funded silvopasture at a larger scale.
"Silvopasture, within the various different approaches for sequestering carbon via natural systems, is one of the pathways with the most promising potential for scale. And carbon finance has a role to play in financing that solution," Julia Strong, executive director of the Symbiosis Coalition, told Reuters.
The coalition, whose members include Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google, Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) and [USN:L1N45B037 TEXT:"Salesforce"] (CRM.N) , focuses on long-term carbon offset contracts, with pledges for more than 20 million tons of offsets by 2030.
Working Trees plants rows of commercial timber and native tree species directly into existing cattle pasture, leaving space for grazing.
The company says the model improves cattle productivity while generating future timber revenue that encourages landowners to maintain the systems after carbon-credit income declines.
"This project and the potential to scale to millions of hectares in this part of Brazil is a really exciting opportunity to showcase what good looks like," Strong said, adding that Working Trees had demonstrated the model through a pilot project.
Working Trees Chief Executive Leif Gonzales-Kramer said the long-term purchase commitments were critical to unlocking investment for such projects.
"If you believe that the world will continue to eat beef and that the world will take climate action seriously, the only way that you can actually achieve both at the same time is through silvopasture," he said.
Brazil's [USN:L6N45U0TV TEXT:"nascent carbon market"] has attracted increased interest [USN:L1N45B037 TEXT:"from investors and lenders"] as companies seek high-quality carbon-removal projects to meet climate goals.
Technology companies, in particular, are looking for ways to [USN:L1N3WI19U TEXT:"offset emissions"] linked to the rapid expansion of energy-intensive artificial intelligence infrastructure. Some critics, however, say the offsets allow polluters to avoid reducing their emissions.

items.title: Myanmar authorities release rare images of Aung San Suu Kyi
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Myanmar's military-backed government on Monday released rare photographs of the country's imprisoned former leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, saying that officials had delivered her books and letters from Britain's King Charles.
items.body:
Myanmar's military-backed government on Monday released rare photographs of the country's imprisoned former leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, saying that officials had delivered her books and letters from Britain's King Charles.
The government officials delivered two books — "The Land Gardeners: Soil to Table" and "Soil: The World at Our Feet" — along with a sealed envelope and a diplomatic communication sent by King Charles, according to a social media post from Myanmar's presidential spokesperson
Suu Kyi, 81, has been detained since February 2021, when the military ousted her administration and arrested civilian leaders in early-morning raids
The delivery shows rare foreign contact with Suu Kyi, whose whereabouts and health have been difficult to determine after the 2021 coup. No foreign leader or envoy has publicly met with her despite requests
The Nobel laureate was [USN:L6N41D0F6 TEXT:"moved to house arrest"] in April this year, following an election held under military rule that installed coup leader Min Aung Hlaing as president
In August, she [USN:L1N440037 TEXT:"met with a representative"] of the International Committee of the Red Cross following years of questions over her health and wellbeing
She is currently serving an [USN:L1N41004U TEXT:"18-year prison sentence"] at a designated residence for a litany of offences — ranging from incitement and corruption to election fraud and violating a state secrets law — all of which she denies

items.summary: Amazon.com is introducing a new tool that allows its custom AI chips to run code written in the most popular AI coding language without modification, seeking to erode the advantage that underpins Nvidia's dominance in the AI computing market.
items.body:
Amazon.com (AMZN.O) is introducing a new tool that allows its custom AI chips to run code written in the most popular AI coding language without modification, seeking to erode the advantage that underpins Nvidia's (NVDA.O) dominance in the AI computing market.
Shares of the company were up 5% in morning trading, with Morgan Stanley naming Amazon a "top pick".
TorchNeuron lets developers run code written in a language called PyTorch on Amazon's Trainium AI chips with a single configuration change and no rewriting needed, according to Amazon's Annapurna Labs chip unit.
Amazon, which plans to announce the software at a developer conference in Silicon Valley on Monday, said the software will be publicly released as a free and open-source offering.
PyTorch, the open-source framework stewarded by Meta (META.O) , is used by most AI developers. Nvidia has spent more than a decade on its software tool called Cuda that makes PyTorch code run well on Nvidia chips.
Other cloud computing players such as Google (GOOGL.O) , which also has its own custom AI chips, are also working to lure away developers from Nvidia [USN:L6N3XL15R TEXT:"with better PyTorch tools"].
Colin Brace, vice president of software for Annapurna Labs, said the move was aimed at reducing the number of steps AI developers must take to try Amazon's in-house chips.
"This has been about meeting customers where they're at," he told Reuters in an interview.
Brace said more than 30 early customers — spanning robotics, world models and voice AI — are using the new software, and that the switch to Amazon's chips can result in steep cost savings.

OSLO, Oct 19 : Norway's planned social media ban for children will include provisions targeting "harmful platforms", the government said on Monday, naming messaging and gaming services Roblox, Snapchat and TikTok among those affected.
The Nordic country said in April it would present a bill in parliament by the end of the year to ban children from using social media until they turn 16, making technology companies responsible for age verification. It did not name any platforms at the time.
Several European nations are seeking to rein in children's social media use after Australia took the lead with the world's first ban on under-16s last December, which included apps such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube.
Norway's government said in a statement on Monday that its bill was intended to address the full range of risks children face on social media and that it would affect "many platforms".

The ministry went on to define what it called harmful platforms as "social media that, through its design, features or content, poses a risk to children's emotional, cognitive or physical development or safety."
"The government believes that platforms such as TikTok, Roblox, and Snapchat will be covered by the law," it said.

items.title: What's behind Egypt's move towards possible military involvement in Saudi-Yemen conflict?
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Egypt's parliament is expected to vote next week on whether to authorise the armed forces to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen's Houthis if Riyadh requests its support.
items.body:
[USN:L8N46306J TEXT:"Egypt's parliament"] is expected to vote [USN:L6N4650W2 TEXT:"next week"] on whether to authorise the armed forces to help defend [USN:L1N4610OX TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"] against attacks by Yemen's Houthis if Riyadh requests its support.
The move would bring the Arab world's most populous country closer to direct military involvement in the widening conflicts unleashed by the US-Israeli air assault on Iran in February.
President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi [USN:L1N46401H TEXT:"requested the approval"] in a speech on Saturday, saying Egypt would "never, never forget our brothers in the Gulf" and telling Saudi Arabia's leaders that Cairo would "take any measure to protect you".
Like the [USN:L6N4610JI TEXT:"Gulf states"] that have come under attack from Tehran in the Iran war , Egypt is a longstanding partner in the US-led security order that is being tested by the conflict.
WHAT IS EGYPT'S STANCE ON THE IRAN WAR? Sisi's comments marked a clear escalation from the more measured tone authorities have tended to adopt since the Iran war started. Though Egypt has repeatedly voiced strong support for its Gulf allies, Cairo has stopped short of publicly committing itself to a direct combat role in the conflict.
In May, the presence of Egyptian Rafale fighter jets in the United Arab Emirates was disclosed in Emirati state media coverage of an official visit by Sisi. Egyptian coverage of the visit did not mention the deployment. When Saudi Arabia signed a [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"joint defence agreement"] with Turkey and Pakistan in August, Egypt did not join, though it said it was considering it.
The tone started to shift after [USN:L1N46209G TEXT:"the Houthis"] stepped up attacks on Saudi oil and other infrastructure. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman last month visited Egypt, where he discussed the need to ensure freedom and security of navigation in the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] and the Red Sea, on which both countries have long coastlines.
WHAT'S AT STAKE FOR EGYPT? Egypt's economic stability has long been tied up with the oil-producing Gulf. Remittances from Egyptian expatriate workers there are an important source of foreign currency and income for families back home at a time of double-digit inflation worsened by surging food and fuel prices.
Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf countries have been among Sisi's key financial backers, providing tens of billions of dollars of aid, central bank deposits and investments since the army overthrew President Mohamed Morsi, a senior Muslim Brotherhood figure, in 2013.
"We can never forget how our brothers in the Gulf states stood by Egypt during that period," Sisi said in his speech.
Saudi Arabia has a $5.3 billion deposit at Egypt's central bank due this month along with $267 million in interest, central bank data shows.
WHAT ABOUT SECURITY? Growing security concerns have also pushed Cairo towards a more active stance, analysts say. A [USN:L6N43V132 TEXT:"drone strike"] on two gas vessels at the Mediterranean port city of Damietta in July underscored that Egypt could not expect to keep itself fully isolated from the conflict.
"I think they realise that they can't be on the sidelines about this indefinitely," said H. A. Hellyer, a scholar at the Royal United Services Institute think tank.
For the authorities, the economic and security concerns were "one and the same," he said.
Saudi Arabia and Egypt also have a shared interest in securing shipping through the Red Sea, an outlet for Saudi oil blocked from leaving the [USN:L1N4100GE TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"]. Egypt earns billions of dollars a year from fees on Suez Canal traffic. These overlapping concerns mean "Saudi Arabia's security constitutes a dimension of Egyptian national security," said Sherif Aref, an Egyptian political researcher and journalist.
WHAT SORT OF MILITARY DOES EGYPT BRING TO THE TABLE? Egypt has one of the Arab world's largest armed forces, with hundreds of thousands of active personnel and large air, land and naval inventories, according to military analysts. Egypt sources equipment from a range of countries, and its air force operates US-made F-16s, French Rafales and Russian-made MiG-29s.
Egypt receives about $1.3 billion a year in US military aid, which helps fund its purchases of American military equipment. Washington waived [USN:L6N45N0G9 TEXT:"human rights conditions"] on a tranche of the funds this year after what it called Cairo's "helpful role" since the Iran war began.
In the years after the 2011 uprising that ousted President Hosni Mubarak, the armed forces fought a counterinsurgency campaign against Islamist militants in the Sinai Peninsula. Egypt also contributed air and naval forces to the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015, and conducted airstrikes against Islamic State targets in Libya during that country’s civil war.
Egypt has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War, when its troops joined the US-led coalition to drive Iraqi forces from Kuwait. Nearly three decades earlier, President Gamal Abdel Nasser had sent Egyptian forces into Yemen in a costly intervention later compared to the US involvement in the Vietnam War.
WHAT SORT OF SUPPORT IS LIKELY? Sisi's speech and subsequent statements have not specified what sort of military forces, if any, Egypt would ultimately intend to send. A deployment of Egyptian troops inside Yemen itself is unlikely, military analysts say.
More likely interventions might include air defence and naval support, said Samir Ragheb, a retired Egyptian military officer who heads the Arab Foundation for Development and Strategic Studies think tank.
"The threats, missiles and drones, require air defence and air forces," he said, adding that the navy could be used for protecting ships, naval operations against piracy and protecting the Saudi coastline.
Still, the entry of another large conventional Arab military would not "suddenly solve the Houthi problem", said Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's College London.
"The Houthis are difficult precisely because they generate disproportionate effect through missiles, drones, dispersed forces and geography. Egypt cannot bomb that problem away," he said.
"What Cairo can do is strengthen Saudi resilience, improve Red Sea control, share the defensive burden and increase the political cost of continued attacks."

Oct 19 : AI-linked stocks bounced back on Monday from a bruising selloff last week as yields on government bonds dropped and crude oil prices eased, while CoreWeave gained following a rating upgrade.
Its shares were up 2.4 per cent in choppy trading after losing a quarter of their value last week as the neocloud company's $50 billion debt triggered a crisis of confidence, sparking a global selloff across AI and tech stocks.
"It's going to continue to be a factor, it's going to be a constant push-pull over time," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital.
Goldman Sachs upgraded CoreWeave to "buy" from "neutral", saying tight computing capacity and the company's performance advantage over rival neocloud firms should lift annual recurring revenue per megawatt over the next two years. The brokerage said the recent pullback is a buying opportunity.

The yield on CoreWeave's bond maturing in 2031 fell 19.5 basis points to 15.13 per cent, easing from more than 16 per cent last week, according to Tradeweb data.
Neocloud rival Nebius Group rose 3.4 per cent after tumbling more than 31 per cent in the past two weeks. Data center operators Applied Digital and IREN gained 8.5 per cent and 5 per cent, respectively.
"You could certainly see a dead cat bounce today and maybe some continuation tomorrow, but it doesn't change the fact that the bond market is very skeptical about continuing to finance this without demanding higher and higher yields," added Hayes.
The AI trade stumbled last week after a hot inflation reading raised bets for interest-rate hikes, fuelling concerns that heavily indebted AI companies could face higher borrowing costs.
Morgan Stanley expects total AI investment to surge to $1.6 trillion in 2027 and $1.8 trillion in 2028.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped more than 11 per cent last week, with chip stocks among the hardest hit in the AI rout.
The index has shed around $2 trillion in market value during an eight-session losing streak through Friday. It was last up 2.4 per cent, on course to snap its longest losing streak since October 2008.
Intel climbed 4.5 per cent after J.P. Morgan upgraded the stock to "neutral" from "underweight", saying rising agentic AI workloads and tight supplies of advanced chips could support positive earnings estimate revisions through 2027.
Nvidia added 1.5 per cent, AMD gained 3.6 per cent and Broadcom advanced 2.4 per cent, after all three sold off sharply last week.
Memory-chip maker Micron Technology climbed 4.2 per cent after sliding nearly 15 per cent last week. Data-storage firms Sandisk, Western Digital and Seagate gained after steep declines last week.
Earnings from megacap technology companies and hyperscalers could be the next test for the AI trade that powered Wall Street to record highs earlier this year, as investors look for evidence that earnings growth can offset concerns over valuations, debt and interest rates.
Facebook-parent Meta Platforms and Elon Musk-led Tesla and SpaceX will report results later this week.
Semiconductor companies Lam Research, Texas Instruments and Western Digital, are also set to report quarterly results.
"The question this quarter is not whether AI will continue to grow, it's whether investors are still willing to pay a premium for that growth," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets.

Elon Musk promises a SpaceX share to every child in the US next year

New Delhi: Elon Musk has promised to distribute a share of SpaceX to each child in the United States of America next year. His announcement on X came hours after AI giant Anthropic detailed plans to dedicate a significant portion of its equity to serve the public.

“Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many,” Musk wrote in a post on X.

SpaceX shares are currently trading at around $146-147. With roughly 72–73 million people under the age of 18 in the US, this one-time gift would be valued at approximately $10.5 to $10.7 billion according to current prices. However, Musk is yet to release details on eligibility, distribution mechanics, tax treatment, or any restrictions on the shares.

Show Full Article

SpaceX was founded by Musk in March 2002, and he currently holds a 48.4 per cent stake in the company, representing roughly 6.42 billion shares valued at over $860 billion to $900 billion.

Also read: France’s unrest reaches the Louvre as protesters block the iconic museum

Following Anthropic’s footsteps
Musk’s charity pledge followed Anthropic’s announcement on Sunday, a day before his announcement.

Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, structured as a public benefit corporation, said it would commit 5 per cent of its shares (subject to stockholder approval) to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund.

“It will start off with 5 per cent of our shares. For every 50 per cent increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2 per cent, subject to our board’s discretion,” they wrote in a post detailing the scheme. “In total, this means that roughly 20 per cent of Anthropic’s shares are committed to public good.”

The post highlighted that the co-founders have already pledged to donate 80 per cent of their equity, and nearly half the employees are also donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program. The company emphasized that none of the equity held by the fund will be used for lobbying or will be given to political parties.

“I recommend giving the shares directly to the public,” Musk had written in response to Anthropic’s post adding , “This is what I will be doing.”

His follow-up post on Monday specified that children in the US would be the initial recipients of SpaceX equity.

The announcements arrive amid heightened scrutiny of AI companies over safety risks, job displacement, the environmental footprint of large-scale computing, and other concerns.

Despite the charitable pledge, Musk has a history of high-profile pledges that he does not follow through with, Bloomberg noted.

In October 2021, Musk challenged the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) to provide an open-source spending plan showing how $6 billion of his wealth could solve world hunger. When they gave him a breakdown, Musk did not follow through with his promise.

(Edited by Janaki Pande)

Nine Years, Made Possible by Readers

items.title: Senator Schumer urges FCC to reject conservative group's bid to use political AI-generated robocalls
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer on Monday urged the Federal Communications Commission not to approve a petition to allow political AI-generated robocalls from conservative political group Club for Growth ahead of the November congressional elections.
items.body:
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer on Monday urged the Federal Communications Commission not to approve a petition to allow political AI-generated robocalls from conservative political group Club for Growth ahead of the November congressional elections.
"Under this change, campaigns could use their opponents’ voice to send out a message that is, at best, disingenuous and, at worst, a blatant lie," Schumer said.
The comment period expires on Monday.
FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez, a Democrat who has opposed the petition, said Monday on CNN the FCC could act in the coming days and just two weeks ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
A spokesperson for the FCC said the agency is not planning to grant the petition. "There is no one at the FCC that has expressed any interest in moving to an order on this or any of the petitions and there are zero plans to so," the spokesperson said.
"There is absolutely no excuse to relax these standards and allow special interests to flood our cellphone lines with deepfakes or dark-money-funded AI voices," Schumer said.
The group, which is spending millions of dollars ahead of the November US congressional elections , earlier asked the FCC to allow it to make political calls to cell phones "using an artificial or prerecorded voice - including an AI-generated voice - without obtaining prior express consent."
Club for Growth President David McIntosh said in a statement earlier this month that the group wants "the FCC to treat First Amendment-protected political speech the same way it already treats wireless calls about package deliveries, bank accounts, and doctor's appointments."
The group, which backs conservative economic views on taxes, regulations and cutting the size of government, plans to spend $175 million in the midterm congressional elections, it said on its website.
The FCC, in describing the petition, said the system "uses a perfunctory human being for the sole purpose of clicking on a ‘send’ or similarly termed button to transmit thousands of text messages per hour."
A number of public interest groups have urged the FCC not to grant the petition.
Schumer noted that in 2024, the FCC proposed fining a political consultant $6 million over fake robocalls that mimicked then President Joe Biden's voice, urging New Hampshire voters not to vote in that state's Democratic primary.

items.title: Disc Medicine's late-stage win clears path for approval of sun-allergy pill
items.author: Padmanabhan Ananthan
items.creator: Padmanabhan Ananthan
items.summary: Disc Medicine said on Monday its experimental pill for a rare disease helped patients spend more time in sunlight without pain, sending its shares surging 35% in early trading.
items.body:
Disc Medicine (IRON.O) said on Monday its experimental pill for a rare disease helped patients spend more time in sunlight without pain, sending its shares surging 35% in early trading.
The late-stage trial success sets the stage for Disc to resubmit its application for an FDA review of bitopertin after the regulator [USN:L4N3Z91U2 TEXT:"turned down"] the drug earlier this year. Disc plans to submit the new data by year-end, supporting potential approval and launch around mid-2027.
The FDA had then cited a lack of a clear link between the reduction in patients' protoporphyrin levels and their tolerance to sunlight.
Bitopertin is being developed to treat erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), an inherited blood disorder in which a substance called protoporphyrin IX (PPIX) builds up in the blood and makes patients extremely sensitive to sunlight, causing painful skin reactions on exposure.
"We believe the breadth and consistency of the topline findings leave limited residual uncertainty around approvability," Truist analyst Danielle Brill said.
In the trial, which enrolled 183 patients aged 12 and older, those who took bitopertin had 41.4% lower PPIX levels compared to placebo. In the sixth month of treatment, they also gained 12.2 more hours per month of pain-free time in sunlight.
The drug also significantly decreased the number of phototoxic reactions, which are painful skin reactions triggered by light.
"These results mark a significant scientific advancement in EPP ... I expect these results will permanently change the focus of drug development in this field," CEO John Quisel said on a conference call.
Patients with EPP now mainly manage the disease by avoiding sunlight or by using Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals' (CUV.AX) implant, Scenesse.
BMO analysts estimate peak sales of $1.7 billion for bitopertin and expect early uptake from patients already on therapy through the FDA's expanded access program.

items.title: 北朝鮮、韓国向け拡声器放送の再開検討─与正氏＝ＫＣＮＡ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ソウル １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ソウル １９日 ロイター] - 北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の妹である金与正党総務部長は１９日、同国が韓国との境界線付近への戦術兵器の追加配備や拡声器による放送の再開を検討していると述べた。

国営メディアの朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）を通じた声明で、「現在、境界線の南側状況は非常に不安定だ」とし、「韓国軍の好戦分子たちは、自動小銃や大口径機関銃で警告射撃を行うなど、わが国の軍人の安全を深刻に脅かしている」と語った。

２０２４年４月に北朝鮮が南北軍事境界線（ＤＭＺ）付近の要塞化を開始して以来、韓国との緊張が高まっている。

韓国軍は１０月５日、北朝鮮が今年、地雷やフェンスの設置のために最大７０００人の作業員を動員し、境界線を越える事件が約５０件発生したと発表した。

韓国側は、先月に北朝鮮の地雷が原因でＤＭＺ付近で爆発が発生し、韓国軍兵士２人が重傷を負ったと述べ、北朝鮮に要塞化作業の中止を求めた。

ソウルにある慶南大学極東研究所のイム・ウルチョル教授は「韓国軍は北朝鮮の要塞化工事に対し、警戒態勢を強化し、警告射撃や拡声器による放送を行っている」と指摘。「北朝鮮は、韓国によるこうした警告活動がＤＭＺ付近の緊張を高めたり、軍事衝突を引き起こしたりするのではないかと懸念しているようだ」と語った。

与正氏は、８月１日から１０月１７日までの間に、韓国側が２８７０回の拡声器による警告を行い、２０１発の警告射撃を行ったと述べた。

韓国側は、北朝鮮の要塞化工事に対抗するためのＤＭＺ付近での活動に関するデータを公表していない。

与正氏は「現在の状況に対処するため、わが軍の指導部は、不測の事態に備える先制的・抑止的措置として、境界線沿いにさらなる戦術的打撃手段を配備することや、韓国に対する拡声器放送を再開すること、その他必要かつ適切な措置について検討している」と述べた。

韓国国防省からは、直ちにコメントを得ることはできなかった。

items.title: Milan luxury shops close for fear of further unrest, govt prepares new crackdown
items.author: Elisa Anzolin
items.creator: Elisa Anzolin
items.summary: Shops in central Milan closed early and boarded up their windows on Monday, fearing a new wave of unrest after two days of protests that saw demonstrators clash with police, loot stores and vandalise property.
items.body:
Shops in central Milan closed early and boarded up their windows on Monday, fearing a new wave of unrest after two days of protests that saw demonstrators clash with police, loot stores and vandalise property.
Most stores in Milan's Via Montenapoleone luxury shopping district, home to brands including Chanel, Tiffany and Dior, had removed merchandise from their windows as a precaution, while police patrolled the street and a handful of tourists looked on.
Several hundred hooded protesters, many believed to be minors, set bins ablaze and looted shops in the city centre over the weekend after an initially peaceful demonstration on Saturday over poor public services and rising costs.
Among the stores ransacked were sports retailers Decathlon and Arc'teryx and mobile phone operator Vodafone, television footage showed. Stores such as clothing brands Levi's and Under Armour, as well as Decathlon, covered their shop windows with cardboard and wooden panels.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who faces a national election next year, condemned the violence and chaired a meeting with ministers and security chiefs on Monday to discuss the situation.
The government is planning to introduce measures proposed by the police aimed at preventing and combatting such outbreaks of violence, a gouvernment source said, adding that the proposals would be put to a cabinet meeting expected on Tuesday.
Corriere della Sera newpaper said Meloni was considering extending preventive detention for minors and cracking down on youth gangs, bringing forward some provisions contained in an existing security bill currently being examined by parliament.
Italian police said it had detained 271 young people during unrest in Milan on Sunday. Of those taken to police stations, 32 were arrested, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, police said on Monday. A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.
The unrest followed clashes on Saturday in Milan and other northern cities including Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, where 28 protesters were arrested, according to a police report released on Sunday.
The disturbances echoed unrest [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"in neighbouring France"], where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising living costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years.

items.title: Rubio seeks to expand Central Asia ties with pomp-filled Uzbekistan visit
items.author: Gram Slattery, Doina Chiacu
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Doina Chiacu
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with counterparts from five Central Asian nations in Uzbekistan on Monday, a trip that resulted in relatively minor public deliverables, but which US officials have presented as an opportunity to expand American soft power.
items.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with counterparts from five Central Asian nations in Uzbekistan on Monday, a trip that resulted in relatively minor public deliverables, but which US officials have presented as an opportunity to expand American soft power.
Rubio, who arrived in the historic Silk Road city of Samarkand on Sunday night, met in the morning with the foreign ministers of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. In the evening, he dined with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and participated in a US-Uzbekistan business council event.
The Trump administration has portrayed resource-rich Central Asia — wedged between Russia, Iran and China — as a major geopolitical battleground that deserves more attention than it has received under previous administrations. US officials have placed a particular emphasis on trying to secure greater access to the area's rare earth mineral supplies, and Rubio came to Samarkand with more than 200 US business leaders in tow, the State Department said.
"I mean, look, it's competition," Rubio told journalists on Monday morning after strolling through Registan Square, a complex of three imposing, azure-tiled madrassas that date to the Timurid Empire. "We have products, we have companies, they make things, and we just want fair competition and an opportunity."
Upon landing in Samarkand on Sunday night, Rubio was warmly embraced by Uzbekistan's foreign minister, Bakhtiyor Saidov, while two women clad in elaborate gold-and-black traditional dresses presented him with a bouquet. In Registan Square on Monday, Rubio's Uzbek hosts released hundreds of pigeons into the sky and filled the vast space with local pop music.
VISIT COINCIDES WITH CRISIS IN UKRAINE Rubio's trip comes at a fraught time in international affairs, and the secretary has faced questions from reporters about whether traveling to Uzbekistan is the best use of his time.
Speaking to assembled business leaders on Monday night, Rubio appeared to address those criticisms, saying foreign trips were too often designed to resolve immediate crises, rather than build long-term relationships.
"Our focus on a problem region or a problem country or a problem issue in the world still has to be there, but it cannot come at the expense of embracing opportunities," Rubio said. "You have to be able to do both. Certainly, a large country and an influential country like the United States needs to be able to do both."
US-Ukraine relations are at a low point after Washington urged Kyiv earlier in the month to stop striking Russian refineries and agreed to buy Russian diesel in a bid to lower domestic fuel prices ahead of the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"US midterm elections"]. The war with Iran shows little sign of resolution, and US ally Saudi Arabia has entered a disruptive war with Yemen's Houthis.
While European diplomats have often viewed Rubio as more supportive of Ukraine than Trump, in Samarkand he showed no signs of disagreeing with his boss, telling reporters that Zelenskiy should focus on ending the war and denying an assertion by Ukraine's leader that the US had paused intelligence sharing.
There are indications some of the Central Asian nations present, all of which are post-Soviet states, are deepening diplomatic and economic links with Washington.
On Monday, Uzbekistan signed the Artemis Accords, a US-led multilateral agreement that sets non-binding principles and legal guidelines for peaceful space exploration and resource management. The US and Uzbekistan also signed an investment agreement across various sectors that the parties said would total $12 billion when implemented.
But all five nations also maintain significant commercial and diplomatic links with Russia and, to varying extents, China and Iran, a fact that Rubio acknowledged.
"Countries want to have as many relationships as possible," Rubio told reporters while speaking alongside Saida Mirziyoyeva, the daughter of Uzbekistan's president and the head of the presidential office.
"Uzbekistan's been clear: they want to be friends to everybody."

NEW DELHI, Oct 19 : US President Donald Trump's waiver of Russian sanctions eases energy concerns for India, one of the top importers of Russian oil, and may improve the chances of New Delhi and Washington agreeing on a trade deal, besides helping overall ties.
An executive order issued by Trump on Friday waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs — including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas — that had been scheduled to start this week under the legislation known as the Graham Act.
Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States.
The legislation would have exposed Indian goods to stiff tariffs of up to 100 per cent as India is one of the five largest importers of Russian oil and posed a challenge for the Asian nation's energy policies.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration warned last month the new tariff measures on Russia could hurt bilateral ties, adding to diplomatic strain and trade uncertainty.
RUBIO SAYS TRADE DEAL 'VERY CLOSE'
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who arrives in India on Tuesday, said trade talks with New Delhi were a consideration for Trump's decision.
"We are trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now and we are very close to doing that. So, that's one of the things we take into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers," Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan on Monday.
India is the world's third-largest oil importer and consumer. Earlier this year, Russia accounted for nearly half of the country's oil imports, but purchases fell in August and continue to decline.
Persistently cutting Russian oil imports to avoid new US tariffs risks pushing up fuel prices ahead of regional elections in India, or straining government finances.
"For some countries it is very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources," Rubio said.
Rubio's two-day visit to India will include a meeting with foreign minister S. Jaishankar on Tuesday to discuss bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, and defence.
A trade deal between India and the United States has been in the making for months but could not be finalised as talks stalled in part due to complications from the new tariff threat.
"The decision to pause on Russia sanctions could be the confidence-building measure that gives the two sides the negotiating space to get over the final hump," said Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council in Washington.
A trade deal has also been held back because Washington is yet to complete a Section 301 trade investigation into several nations, including India, over alleged excess manufacturing capacity. Section 301 is a US trade law that allows retaliation against unfair foreign trade practices.
Earlier this month, India joined a US-led initiative to act against structural overcapacity, along with a few other nations.
Trade officials in New Delhi last week said an agreement with the US was nearly done and expressed optimism over securing a tariff lower than those of competing countries — a longstanding Indian expectation from the deal. 
"It (the waiver) provides an important opening and at a critical moment" after renewed tensions over the sanctions bill and new US visa policies had put the relationship "in danger of falling into even harder times," Kugelman said.

Source: Reuters

items.title: ロシア大規模攻撃で全土に被害、ゼレンスキー氏「事前警告なし」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Olena Harmash

[キーウ １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Olena Harmash

[キーウ １９日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１９日、ロシアによる夜間の弾道ミサイル攻撃について、同盟国から事前の警告を受けていなかったと明らかにした。また、米国からの重要な物資の一部で供給の遅れが生じていると述べた。

ロシアはこの日の未明にかけて、ここ数カ月見られていなかった広範な攻撃を実施。攻撃は東部ハルキウ州とドニプロ州から、南部オデーサ州、西部ボルィーニ州とリウネ州まで広範に及んだ。ウクライナ全土のエネルギーインフラが被害を受け、５０万世帯超が停電に見舞われている。

ゼレンスキー氏によると１０カ所を超えるエネルギー施設が被害を受けた。エネルギー省は復旧作業が進められる中、家庭や企業を対象に計画停電が導入されている。

ロスア軍は首都キーウと周辺地域に弾道ミサイル１６発、ウクライナ全土に２００機を超えるドローン（無人機）を投入。ウクライナ当局者によると、一連の攻撃でキーウとその周辺地域で２人が死亡したほか、中南部の工業都市クリビーリフで２人が死亡した。このほか北東部ハリコフ州では、ロシアのドローン攻撃で子ども３人を含む６人が死亡した。

ウクライナのコレツキー首相によると、攻撃の主な標的はエネルギー部門で、全土で被害が報告された。鉄道駅や医薬品倉庫、商業施設、住宅も被害を受けたという。

＜ゼレンスキー氏「ミサイル攻撃に早期警告なし」＞

ゼレンスキー氏は「夜間に再びロシアの弾道ミサイル攻撃が数波にわたってあり、今回も同盟国から事前警告はなかった」と通信アプリ「テレグラム」に投稿。「ウクライナへの防空用ミサイル供給が阻まれる一方、ロシアには制裁の緩和や先送りが認められている。残念ながら、これは同盟国が現実から目を背けているということだ」とした。

ゼレンスキー氏は、米国からのウクライナ向けの重要な軍事物資の一部の供給が遅延していると明らかにした。遅延は米国防総省レベルで発生しているとの見方を示したが、詳細については言及しなかった。ウクライナはこれまでも、ロシアのミサイル攻撃迎撃に不可欠な米国製の地対空ミサイルシステム「パトリオット」の迎撃ミサイルの確保が難しくなっていると訴えている。

また、防空支援に関する一部の政治的合意が実務レベルで履行されていないとも述べた。

ルビオ米国務長官は、米国がウクライナとの情報共有の一部を停止したことを否定している。

ウクライナ空軍の報道官はテレビに対し、夜間の最初の弾道ミサイル攻撃に先立つ警告はなかったが２回目の攻撃の前には情報を受け取ったと指摘。「何らかの理由で、最初の攻撃の際には情報を受け取れなかった。同様の事態は初めてではなく協力国とともに調査している」と語った。

ウクライナ空軍によると、巡航ミサイル４発とドローン２４３機を迎撃した。

＜ロシア、防衛産業施設など標的と表明＞

ロシア国防省は、精密誘導兵器と攻撃用ドローンでウクライナの防衛産業施設、ドローンや巡航ミサイル保管施設、データセンターに「大規模攻撃」を実施したと表明。

ウクライナのコレツキー首相は、ロシアは７月中旬以降、ウクライナのエネルギーインフラを２０００回超攻撃しているとし、過去数年の戦争期間と比べても攻撃を激化させていると指摘。鉄道駅や地下鉄駅、医薬品倉庫、商業施設、住宅建物も被害を受けており、ウクライナ企業が今年に入って被った戦争被害による損失は合計７７億ドルに上るとの試算を示した。

NEW YORK, Oct 19 : Oil prices slipped more than $1 on Monday as investors took profits after prices climbed to multi-month highs last week, while keeping a close watch on conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine and assessing the impact of U.S. waivers on some sanctions and tariffs affecting Russian exports.
Brent crude futures fell $1.72, or 1.6 per cent, to $108.14 a barrel at 1027 a.m. ET  or 1427 GMT, after settling at their highest since May 19 on Friday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude was trading at $100.54 barrel, down 87 cents, or 0.86 per cent, after ending last week at its highest since September 17.
"Ongoing strikes on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz and flows remaining below pre-conflict levels continue to provide support," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said.

An oil tanker caught fire and exploded after striking a naval mine in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said, according to Iranian media.
The increased attacks on commercial vessels cut Gulf crude flows to a seven-day average of about 8.5 million barrels per day last week from more than 20 million bpd the week before, analytics firm Kpler said in a note on Friday. At least 10 confirmed incidents involving commercial vessels were reported last week, Kpler added.
It is not a given that recent higher export volumes out of Hormuz will continue, as Iran will likely further escalate its attacks in the run-up to the November 3 US midterm elections, SEB analyst Bjarne Schieldrop said. 
Egypt said it is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability against Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war.  
Saudi Arabia's civil defense authority issued a series of alerts on Monday warning of potential danger in several areas, including Riyadh, before later saying the threat had passed.
This came after fifty-three people were killed in a Houthi attack and 200 were injured in on a Yemeni government security force training camp in the energy-rich Shabwa province in coastal south-central Yemen on Monday.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order waiving some sanctions and tariffs related to Russian exports.
The waiver comes after Trump struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to export diesel to the United States and other countries — starting at about 2.3 million barrels this month before rising to about 7.6 million barrels monthly. 
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president will take up to 60 days to assess the impact of the sanctions and tariffs on the global economy.
"Trump's move looks like another desperate attempt to keep oil prices in check ahead of the US midterm elections," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insight at Phillip Nova, adding that it does little to address the physical supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, where oil tanker attacks continue.
Despite a US naval blockade of Iranian shipments in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran has managed to export some liquefied petroleum gas and jet fuel since July, shipping intelligence showed and people involved in security said.
In the meantime, OPEC oil output rose in September, a Reuters survey found, led by gains in Saudi Arabia and Iraq.  

Source: Reuters

items.title: Cobre cae por aumento de existencias en la LME y menor preocupación por suministro
items.author: Polina Devitt
items.creator: Polina Devitt
items.summary: Los precios del cobre cayeron el lunes, ya que el aumento de las existencias y el fin de una huelga en una importante mina chilena aliviaron las preocupaciones sobre el suministro.
items.body:
Los precios del cobre cayeron el lunes, ya que el aumento de las existencias y el fin de una huelga en una importante mina chilena aliviaron las preocupaciones sobre el suministro.
* A las 1600 GMT, el precio del cobre de referencia a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) perdió un 0,4%, a 14.342 dólares por tonelada.
* Las existencias de cobre disponibles en los almacenes registrados en la LME tocaron un pico de dos meses de 147.450 toneladas tras la entrada de 8.225 toneladas en los almacenes estadounidenses, según mostraron los datos diarios de la bolsa.
* Las existencias de cobre fuera de Estados Unidos han caído en los últimos meses, ya que los operadores desviaron los envíos hacia ese país ante la posibilidad de que se impusieran aranceles a las importaciones de cobre refinado, lo que contribuyó a que los precios tocaran un máximo histórico de 14.875 dólares el 10 de septiembre.
* Daniel Ghali, del Deutsche Bank, afirmó que la amenaza de los aranceles estadounidenses forma parte de un cambio estratégico más amplio impulsado por preocupaciones de seguridad nacional en torno a la concentración de las cadenas de suministro de minerales críticos, más que de un riesgo político puntual.
* Asimismo, añadió en una nota que, incluso si se disiparan las preocupaciones sobre los aranceles, los costos de transporte y las fricciones del mercado seguirían desincentivando las exportaciones a gran escala desde Estados Unidos.
* Por el lado de la oferta, los trabajadores de la mina Centinela, de Antofagasta, pusieron fin a una huelga que había comenzado el 7 de octubre.
* En otros metales básicos, el aluminio subió un 0,7%, a 3.021,5 dólares la tonelada; el zinc ganó un 0,8%, a 3.721 dólares; el plomo mejoró un 0,3%, a 1.894,5 dólares; el estaño avanzó un 1%, a 50.860 dólares; y el níquel sumó un 1,3%, a 15.555 dólares.

items.title: Trump geothermal lease sale collides with planned Nevada solar farms
items.author: Nichola Groom
items.creator: Nichola Groom
items.summary: The US Interior Department's sale of geothermal leases in Nevada this week will include thousands of acres overlapping major planned solar projects fromNextEra Energy and other developers, according to federal documents.
items.body:
The US Interior Department's sale of geothermal leases in Nevada this week will include thousands of acres overlapping major planned solar projects from NextEra Energy (NEE.N) and other developers, according to federal documents.
On Tuesday, the Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management is scheduled to auction 83 parcels totaling 265,691 acres to geothermal developers. NextEra, the world's largest owner of solar and wind generation, asked the agency earlier this year to "remove, defer or reconfigure" three proposed geothermal parcels.
President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:S0N3RO0B5 TEXT:"promoted"] geothermal energy as a source of always-on electricity while largely [USN:L1N3X1119 TEXT:"excluding"] wind and solar from a broad effort to accelerate federal permitting.
In comments submitted to the agency during review of the sale, NextEra said the parcels in question overlap roughly 6,000 acres, or about 60%, of its planned 1,000-megawatt Sawtooth Energy Center in Nye County, Nevada.
BLM declined NextEra's request in August, saying federal lands are managed for multiple uses.
Maps published on the BLM website in August show overlaps involving six proposed geothermal parcels and four major planned solar developments in the Nevada desert. One parcel, which overlaps entirely with NextEra's Sawtooth project, did not appear on the auction website and appeared to have been recently removed from the sale.
NextEra, based in Juno Beach, Florida, said in its comments that the overlap could "create a foreseeable conflict" with its pending application.
"NextEra must collaborate with any potential lessee and adjust its operations accordingly to avoid land use conflicts," the agency said. BLM added that if NextEra's project is approved first, it would have the "senior right" and a geothermal development would have to avoid impacts on its project.
Another solar developer, Dallas-based Leeward Renewable Energy, said a geothermal parcel overlaps about 735 acres of its proposed Lone Mountain solar project in Esmeralda County.
It urged the agency to recognize the overlap "and the non-exclusive nature of any future geothermal lessee's development rights."
The agency added a description and maps of the overlapping projects to its sale documents. They include the proposed 300-MW Nivloc solar project being developed by Invenergy and Arevia Power's 1,500-MW Gold Dust solar project.
Along with Lone Mountain, those projects were part of the Esmeralda 7 development, a proposed complex of seven solar farms on 62,000 acres. BLM canceled the environmental review for the complex in 2025 but said the projects may reapply for federal approval individually.
NextEra, Leeward and BLM did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

items.title: VinFast's overseas push lifts quarterly revenue as restructuring gains trim net loss
items.author: Prathik Jayaprakash, Phuong Nguyen
items.creator: Prathik Jayaprakash, Phuong Nguyen
items.summary: Vietnamese electric-vehicle maker VinFast reported an 85.5% jump in second-quarter revenue on Monday, as a one-off $1.18 billion gain from transferring manufacturing assets cut its net loss but its operating loss almost tripled.
items.body:
Vietnamese electric-vehicle maker VinFast (VFS.O) reported an 85.5% jump in second-quarter revenue on Monday, as a one-off $1.18 billion gain from transferring manufacturing assets cut its net loss but its operating loss almost tripled.
The company made public a [USN:L6N41Q0P5 TEXT:"restructuring plan"] in May, including the transfer of manufacturing assets worth about $530 million to a purchaser group that would assume roughly $6.9 billion of debt.
During the second quarter, VinFast recorded a gain from discontinued operations of about $1.18 billion, largely related to the asset transfer. Completed in September, it reduced the company's net loss by about 93% from a year earlier to around $54.65 million.
The operating loss, however, was $1.16 billion in the second quarter, rising 198% from the same time a year earlier.
VinFast shares, listed on the Nasdaq, were down about 1.6% in pre-market trading.
The company was founded in 2017 and became fully focused on EVs in 2022. It said in April it aimed to achieve positive EBITDA by the end of next year.
INTERNATIONAL AMBITIONS Pham Nhat Quan Anh, CEO and chair of VinFast, said in a statement the priorities were to scale up production in international markets including the Philippines, Indonesia and India, while continuing "strategic expansion" across the United States, Europe, and the Middle East.
Quarterly revenue rose to 30.3 trillion dong ($1.17 billion) from a year earlier, helped by stronger sales in Vietnam and growing contributions from high-growth overseas markets including India, Indonesia and the Philippines, the company said.
It added VinFast delivered 70,085 cars in the second quarter, a quarterly increase of 20%, of which 6% went to its related parties.
As it seeks to capture market share across the world, VinFast has expanded its product lineup.
Last month, it launched the VF Wild pickup, a range-extended electric vehicle, in Vietnam, and has plans to introduce the model to overseas markets next year.
($1 = 25,892.0000 dong)

items.title: Yémen-Cinquante-trois morts dans une attaque houthie contre un camp militaire gouvernemental
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cinquante-trois personnes ont été tuées lundi et 200 blessées dans une attaque des rebelles houthis, soutenus par l'Iran, contre un camp d'entraînement militaire du gouvernement yéménite dans la province de Chabwa, dans l'est du Yémen, selon des responsables gouvernementaux.
items.body:
Cinquante-trois personnes ont été tuées lundi et 200 blessées dans une attaque des rebelles houthis, soutenus par l'Iran, contre un camp d'entraînement militaire du gouvernement yéménite dans la province de Chabwa, dans l'est du Yémen, selon des responsables gouvernementaux.
S'exprimant sous couvert d'anonymat, ces responsables ont ajouté que les Houthis avaient tiré trois missiles balistiques sur les forces de sécurité, alors en plein exercice.
Le porte-parole militaire des Houthis, Yahya Saree, a confirmé sur la plate-forme X que ce camp d'entraînement, exploité d'après lui par les forces saoudiennes, avait bien été pris pour cible.
Les autorités saoudiennes n'ont pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire.
Une vidéo vérifiée par Reuters et tournée dans la province de Chabwa, riche en ressources énergétiques, montre des blessés et des corps ensanglantés éparpillés sur le sol.
Les Houthis et les forces gouvernementales yéménites, soutenues par une coalition internationale emmenée par l'Arabie saoudite, ont repris les combats au cours de ces derniers mois.
Cinq mois après le début de la guerre déclenchée par les bombardements des Etats-Unis et d'Israël en Iran, les Houthis avaient annoncé en juillet dernier un blocus maritime de l'Arabie saoudite et ont entrepris de renforcer leur contrôle du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, en mer Rouge, voie cruciale - comme le détroit d'Ormuz - pour les livraisons énergétiques mondiales.
Le mouvement chiite a effectué en septembre une avancée éclair le long du littoral du Yémen, prenant la ville de Mokha, dans le sud-ouest du pays.
Au début du mois, les forces armées gouvernementales yéménites ont annoncé avoir lancé une "[USN:L8N45R15C TEXT:"offensive stratégique"]" sur Sanaa, la capitale du Yémen, afin de reprendre le contrôle de la ville des mains des rebelles houthis.
Le conflit au Yémen a éclaté après la prise de Sanaa par les Houthis en 2014, ce qui a poussé une coalition menée par l’Arabie saoudite à intervenir l’année suivante pour rétablir le gouvernement et chasser le groupe soutenu par l’Iran.
Les combats se sont rapidement enlisés dans une impasse sanglante, la plupart des lignes de front étant gelées. Un cessez-le-feu conclu en 2022 s'est maintenu jusqu’à l'été dernier.
items.raw_description: Cinquante-trois personnes ont été tuées lundi et 200 blessées dans une attaque des rebelles houthis, soutenus par l'Iran, contre un camp d'entraînement militaire du gouvernement yéménite dans la province de Chabwa, dans l'est du Yémen, selon des responsables gouvernementaux.

items.title: 中国人民銀、翌日物リバースレポ金利を主要政策金利に検討中
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [北京／上海 １９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[北京／上海 １９日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が、主要政策金利を翌日物リバースレポ金利に切り替えることを検討している。国営メディアが１９日に報じた。金融政策の伝達メカニズムを改善し、経済を下支えすることを目的とした方針転換となる。

中国では２０２４年以来、７日物リバースレポ金利が主要政策金利として機能してきた。

人民銀が運営する「金融新聞」によると、人民銀の潘功勝総裁は、この主要政策金利の変更は人民銀による短期金利のコントロール精度を高める取り組みの一環だとした。

同紙によると、北京で開催された主要な金融フォーラムで、潘氏は「現在、銀行間翌日物レポ金利は事実上、人民銀の金融政策における目標金利となっている」と発言。「この金利は短期流動性の需給を敏感に反映しており、近年はより高い安定性を示している」と語り、翌日物金利を主要金利とすることで金利管理がより精密になるとした。

この政策転換により、人民銀は流動性状況をより的確にコントロールできるようになり、その政策枠組みは世界の他の中央銀行とより整合性を持つようになる。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）などの中央銀行は、イールドカーブをより確実に定着させるため、すでに翌日物金利を主要な政策金利として採用している。

発表後、中国の３０年物国債利回りは１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）以上低下した。

国泰君安国際のチーフエコノミスト、周浩氏は「金融政策の枠組みが海外と整合することになり、人民元の国際化を推進する上でよりスムーズになるだろう」と述べた。

金融情報サービス大手の中誠信国際のチーフマクロアナリスト、王青氏は、翌日物リバースレポの実際の運用金利は人民銀が切り替えを行う際に発表されるとし、今回の変更は利下げに相当するものではないと指摘した。

中国のインターバンク市場は潤沢な資金供給が続いている。翌日物レポ金利の平均は約１．２５％と約５カ月ぶりの低水準付近にあり、人民銀の翌日物リバースレポ操作における借入コストとして報じられている水準にほぼ沿っている。これは、現在１．４％となっている７日物リバースレポ金利を下回っている。

今回の変更は中国の金融構造の変化とも整合する。中国では、債券や株式を通じた直接金融が従来型の銀行融資を上回り、新規資金調達の主要な供給源となりつつあり、与信配分も不動産など与信依存度の高いセクターから徐々に離れつつある。

翌日物リバースレポ操作は、人民銀の政策手段に加わった最新のツールとして６月下旬に導入された。

翌日物取引は中国のインターバンク短期金融市場におけるレポ取引高の８割超を占めている。

潘氏は、人民銀は貸出金利ベンチマークの改革を推進するため、今後政策指針を示すと述べた。この改革では、融資における最優遇貸出金利（ＬＰＲ）への比較的高い依存度合いを引き下げ、より多様化したベンチマークへの移行を進める。

同氏は、財務体質が良好な一部の企業は金融機関との協議を経て、変動金利融資の基準として銀行間翌日物レポ金利かＬＰＲのいずれかを選択できるようになる可能性があると述べた。

同氏はまた、人民銀は常設貸出ファシリティー（ＳＬＦ）の利用資格を有する金融機関の範囲を拡大し、非銀行系金融機関向けの流動性支援ツールを設ける予定だと述べた。これらの措置は、保険会社やファンド運用会社を含むノンバンク系金融機関への流動性支援を強化することを目的としている。

items.title: FTSE 100 ends lower after three sessions of gains, on weakness in banking, mining stocks
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: London's FTSE 100 closed down on Monday, dragged by Barclays, which fell after a report said that the Bank of England was probing the lender, while weakness in miners added further pressure.
items.body:
London's FTSE 100 closed down on Monday, dragged by Barclays, which fell after a report said that the Bank of England was probing the lender, while weakness in miners added further pressure.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) fell 1.1% to 10,764.69 points after three consecutive sessions of gains. The midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) slipped 0.6%, snapping a six-day winning streak.
Here are more details:
Unilever (ULVR.L) [USN:L6N465106 TEXT:"agreed "]to sell its Welly bandage brand to private-equity firm Forward Consumer Partners, the Wall Street Journal reported after markets closed
Barclays (BARC.L) fell 3.5% as a report by The Financial Times said the Bank of England was examining whether the lender's [USN:L6N4650GN TEXT:"traders misrepresented"] illiquid private credit loans to understate their risk
The broader sector (.FTNMX301010) was down 2.3%
Anglo American (AAL.L) and Glencore (GLEN.L) fell 4.1% and 3.3%, respectively, among the benchmark's biggest drags, as copper prices dipped
Industrial metal miners (.FTNMX551020) , aerospace and defence stocks (.FTNMX502010) and utilities (.FTUB6510) were also down more than 2% each
Investors will be watching for UK September inflation and retail sales figures this week, just as earnings season gets underway
Finance Minister John Healey's first budget speech is due next week. According to media reports, income tax on [USN:L6N4650GK TEXT:"family business transfers"] and [USN:L8N4610PT TEXT:"windfall taxes on banks"] are expected.
Asking prices for British homes rose in October amid signs that rising mortgage rates — caused by the war in Iran — were starting to weigh on affordability and more resilient parts of the market, property website Rightmove said
Serica Energy (SQZ.L) fell 2.6% after flagging a [USN:L4N4650EH TEXT:"further delay to the restart"] of its Triton production vessel and lowering its annual production forecast
Luxury handbag maker Mulberry (MUL.L) gained 2.6% after reporting an 18% jump in first-half [USN:L6N4650F8 TEXT:"sales"].
Volex (VLX.L) bottomed the FTSE 250 after its half-year [USN:L1N465054 TEXT:"trading update"], while Pets at Home (PETSP.L) rose about 6.7% after Peel Hunt's rating upgrade
Risk appetite was subdued in Europe as investors weighed political uncertainty in France
In the broader London market, decliners outnumbered advancers by a 2-to-1 margin

items.title: El oro cae levemente lastrado por fortaleza del dólar y altos rendimientos
items.author: Anushree Mukherjee, Vishak Mathew
items.creator: Anushree Mukherjee, Vishak Mathew
items.summary: Los precios del oro cayeron levemente el lunes, presionados por la fortaleza del dólar y el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, mientras los inversores esperaban la decisión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal la próxima semana, en la que se prevé que el banco central mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios.
items.body:
Los precios del oro cayeron levemente el lunes, presionados por la fortaleza del dólar y el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, mientras los inversores esperaban la decisión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal la próxima semana, en la que se prevé que el banco central mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios.
* El oro al contado caía un 0,5%, a 4.143,91 dólares por onza, a las 1534 GMT. Los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos con vencimiento en diciembre cedían un 0,4%, a 4.163,30 dólares por onza.
* El dólar estadounidense subía levemente, lo que encarecía el oro denominado en dólares para los tenedores de otras divisas, y los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años subían un 0,6%.
* "Existe la preocupación de que los bancos centrales tengan que endurecer aún más sus políticas para controlar la inflación, lo que está dando un nuevo impulso a los rendimientos. Y, dado que los rendimientos se mantienen elevados, los inversores en oro se preguntan si tiene más sentido estar en el mercado de bonos en este momento", dijo Fawad Razaqzada, analista de mercado de Forex.com.
* La Fed subió las tasas de interés un cuarto de punto en septiembre, su primera alza de este año.
* "No se trata solo de si la Fed subirá las tasas la semana que viene o esperará hasta diciembre; el tono de sus orientaciones será determinante. Un mensaje de línea dura podría provocar una mayor debilidad a corto plazo del oro", añadió Razaqzada.
* Según la herramienta FedWatch de la CME, los operadores estiman que hay un 82,8% de probabilidades de que la Fed mantenga las tasas sin cambios este mes, mientras que las expectativas de una subida en diciembre se mantienen en el 90%.
* Aunque el oro suele considerarse una cobertura frente a la inflación, el aumento de las tasas de interés reduce el atractivo de este activo, que no rinde intereses.
* Los inversores también esperan los datos sobre el gasto en consumo personal de Estados Unidos de la próxima semana, el indicador de inflación preferido por el banco central.
* En tanto, los precios del petróleo retrocedían desde su máximo de cinco meses después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, suspendió las sanciones y los aranceles a Rusia, lo que podría dar lugar a un aumento de las exportaciones de combustible ruso.
* Entre otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado subió un 0,4% a 57,24 dólares por onza, el platino ganó un 1% a 1.646 dólares por onza y el paladio sumó un 0,8% a 1.121,14 dólares por onza.

items.title: China's Hansoh Pharma strikes drug deal with Roche worth over $15 billion
items.author: Nichiket Sunil, Patrick Wingrove
items.creator: Nichiket Sunil, Patrick Wingrove
items.summary: China's Hansoh Pharmaceutical said on Monday it has entered into a partnership and licensing deal with Roche potentially worth more than $15 billion that covers a portfolio of antibody-drug conjugate programs.
items.body:
China's Hansoh Pharmaceutical (3692.HK) said on Monday it has entered into a partnership and licensing deal with Roche (ROPC.S) potentially worth more than $15 billion that covers a portfolio of antibody-drug conjugate programs.
As part of the deal with the Swiss drugmaker's unit F. Hoffmann-La Roche, Hansoh will receive an upfront payment of $400 million, a first anniversary payment of $110 million and further milestone payments.
Antibody-drug conjugates are targeted cancer therapies that act like guided missiles, attaching toxic chemotherapy directly to tumor cells while sparing healthy tissue.
Roche currently sells two approved ADCs, Kadcyla and Polivy, that analysts expect to generate a combined 3.5 billion Swiss francs ($4.3 billion) this year, according to LSEG data.
Under the terms of the Hansoh partnership, the Chinese company will lead early development until global Phase Ia clinical trials are complete.
Roche will then take over worldwide development and commercialization, the Chinese company said, excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, where Hansoh retains rights.
Hansoh also has the option to take part in developing up to two programs outside those markets.
Roche said the collaboration, combined with its own research, gave the company the opportunity to advance antibody-drug conjugates as a central component of its next-generation oncology strategy.
The two companies have previously [USN:L6N3VX19N TEXT:"partnered"] on colorectal cancer treatments.
ROCHE STEPPING UP DEALMAKING Facing impending patent cliffs on aging blockbusters, Roche is increasingly turning to external dealmaking to rebuild its pipeline and capture next-generation therapies.
In August, the Swiss drugmaker's Genentech struck a deal with DualityBio worth up to $1 billion for its ADC therapies.
Earlier this month, Roche secured an obesity drug licensing agreement worth up to $1.16 billion with China's Rona Therapeutics, following a January commitment of $100 million upfront for a non-exclusive patent license from Structure Therapeutics covering oral weight-loss drugs.
Teaming up with Hansoh could also fast-track Roche’s route to market. While Roche is advancing oral SERDs like giredestrant in breast cancer, its broader late-stage pipeline faces a notable valley until the end of the decade, making external partnerships essential for near-term momentum.
Drugmakers have struck over a dozen licensing deals with Chinese companies in the past year, highlighted by AstraZeneca’s $18.5 billion [USN:L4N3YV05G TEXT:"obesity drug pact"] with CSPC in January and Bristol Myers Squibb’s $15.2 billion [USN:L4N41P0BH TEXT:"multi-program alliance"] with China’s top drugmaker, Jiangsu Hengrui, in May.
